concerns.title: AC-520 fails pack load on `stage`, `rigor`, `role`, `cost` and `recent_deploy` with no RUNBOOK step or registered spike supplying a passing route; the rigor-monotonicity lint rejects the shipped catalog; and Phase-0 exit (c) is read three ways (Step 3c checks S-BIN alone while design 10.2/10.5 mark S-FACET 'gates Phase 1', registered and unrun)
concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) AC-520, built at 7b, fails pack load unless every `source = "derived"` facet has a scored precision record. Checkpoint 4a requires the derived count to remain eleven ('both are 11'); `stage`, `rigor`, `role`, `cost` and `recent_deploy` have no record and `surfaces` is unscored, and S-FACET's consumer cell (design 1861) covers only `auth`/`surfaces`, `data_migration`, `ui`, `flag_exists` — five of the six can be scored by no registered spike [measured]. Step 8 (6, second lint) nevertheless lists `--facet-provenance` passing, criterion (1) needs a pack to load, and `doctor` refuses an unloadable pack (design §8.10 row 1627; Checkpoint 7d 2107). Separately, ADR-0081 makes a non-monotone rigor family 'an error', RUNBOOK 7b says the lint 'ships in Phase 1 either way and fails on the violation', bisect.toml:12 still keys `applicable_if = "has_repro"` with `min_rigor = "optional"`, and §10.5 marks the removing decision P7-CEIL 'No' for gating Phase 1, 'Awaiting Ryan' [measured]. The RUNBOOK schedules neither S-FACET, nor the registry re-class the register itself names as the other route (1161-1163), nor P7-CEIL. Step 3c checks Phase-0 exit (c) — universal over §10.5 rows marked 'gates Phase 1' — against S-BIN alone ('one genuine shortfall remains'), although design 1789 and 1861 mark S-FACET 'gates Phase 1', unrun, with no F-number and no ADR re-scope; 3c never says whether ADR-0089's authored-not-keyed hedge is the re-scope or S-FACET is a second $0 shortfall. The corpus records each mechanism; it does not record that nothing schedules the decisions between 7b and a loadable pack or catalog. (ii) AC-520 fails load for any `source = "derived"` facet without a scored precision record. `stage`, `rigor`, `role`, `cost` and `recent_deploy` are derived kernel/policy projections with no record and no meaningful one possible; S-FACET's registered consumer covers only `auth`/`surfaces`, `data_migration`, `ui`, `flag_exists`; Checkpoint 4a asserts all eleven stay `source = "derived"` ('both are 11') [measured against spikes/p9/facets.toml]. The register records the honest effect and names the only honest routes (S-FACET, or 'a registry change that moves a deterministic projection out of source = derived'), but no RUNBOOK step re-sources the five, the registry's `source` vocabulary (`human`/`derived`/`llm`) and ADR-0089's classes offer no slot for a deterministic projection, and the Phase-1 exit block nonetheless expects `redkiln lint --facet-provenance` to pass [measured]. Unlike AC-071, whose passing branch is 'zero facets declared llm' (RUNBOOK:2173), AC-520 has no passing branch any Phase-1 step reaches; every `require` row keys on `stage`, so once Step 7b builds the lint as written, no pack loads. (iii) Design 10.2 (c) requires every 10.5 row marked 'gates Phase 1' to carry an F-number or an ADR re-scope, and the register marks S-FACET YES 'for any pack row keyed on those facets' (design:1861); RUNBOOK Step 3c calls the S-BIN half of (c) the one shortfall, Checkpoint 3c greps only for S-BIN, and no step runs or defers S-FACET although RUNBOOK:4 says the design governs [measured]. The register already records (acceptance-criteria.md:1287) that until S-FACET reports, AC-520 fails pack load for the eleven derived facets, five of which (stage, rigor, role, cost, recent_deploy) plus `surfaces` have no F39 figure, so Step 8's second lint (RUNBOOK:2192) has no producing step. For S-BIN, 10.2's Enter column requires exit (a)-(d) while its own May-not column and 10.5:1896 presuppose Phase-1 commits with S-BIN unrun and stop only the ChangeSummary type; HANDOFF:46 says 'Blocking Phase 1'; RUNBOOK:1599 proceeds on '3c answered' while 3c records that neither the finding nor the re-scope ADR exists and the re-scope is 'not the current plan' [measured]. Both readings build the same thing at Step 5 (Checkpoint 5 and 5.3 fence the ChangeSummary work), which is why this is P1 for the pack-rows-over-derived-facets workstream and not P0.

concerns.why_before_step5: (i) [inferred] Steps 5-6 are unaffected; the dependency lands at 7b/7d/8. Both clearing decisions are $0 and must precede 7b or no Phase-1 pack or catalog loads on any path the RUNBOOK provides — the implementer then loosens AC-520 (the collapse AC-071's residual-risk sentence warns of) or takes an unrecorded registry decision. Step 5's banner also requires Step 3c 'answered'; answered against S-BIN alone, the Phase-1 entry check passes with a gating spike neither run nor re-scoped. (ii) Step 5 builds the right thing; the block lands at Step 7b (the lint) and at Phase-1 exit item (6, second lint), which is unreachable by the RUNBOOK's own steps. The only escapes are the 'quiet narrowing' the register forbids or a `source` value nobody has registered. (iii) Step 5's entry gate reads (c) as 'a sentence exists'. Deciding now whether S-FACET runs in Phase 0, or whether AC-520 exempts policy-table derivers (stage/rigor/role/cost), changes what 4a.1 writes into facets.toml and what 7b's lint fixtures assert; under 10.2's letter the first `cargo new` is out of order until S-BIN runs or the re-scope ADR the RUNBOOK explicitly declines to write exists.
concerns.remediation: (i) (a) Before 7b, a companion or successor record to ADR-0089 (never an edit) moving `stage`, `rigor`, `role`, `cost` — and `recent_deploy` under its existing abstention rule — out of `source = "derived"` into a provenance class AC-520 does not gate (e.g. DECLARED), and amending RUNBOOK 4a.1/Checkpoint 4a so the derived count after the edit equals the SCORED count, not eleven; `surfaces` is either re-classed or S-FACET is scheduled as a named Phase-0 step with AC-520 and the pack rows keyed on it as consumer (ADR-0012). State in Step 8 (6b) which facets remain `derived`. (b) Take P7-CEIL before 7b as a recorded catalog decision, or state in 7b which of the two repairs the Phase-1 catalog ships with pending it; correct §10.5's gating cell to 'YES for the catalog as shipped'. (c) Add an S-FACET row to Step 3c's exit-(c) table stating which branch it takes (ADR-0089 as the explicit re-scope, also said in design §10.2's Phase-0 row; or a second $0 shortfall run in Phase 0) and a Checkpoint 3c grep for S-FACET beside the S-BIN one at 906. (ii) Before Step 7b: add to Step 4a a registry change, with anchor assertions, that moves the kernel projections (`stage`, `rigor`, `role`, `cost`) to a new closed `source` value (e.g. `"kernel"`) that AC-072 recognises by name and AC-520 does not gate, recorded as a new ADR in successor scope to ADR-0089 (not an edit); keep `recent_deploy` derived with `deriver = R-recent-deploy-feed-absent` and a record that says NOT MEASURABLE. Correct Checkpoint 4a's 'both are 11' to the reconciled-by-name count. Amend AC-520's domain note and the exit block to say which branch passes. (iii) Take the decision the RUNBOOK defers, as a new ADR (0092 or later - 0090/0091 are claimed; never edit ADR-0008 or ADR-0089): scope S-BIN's gate to the ChangeSummary type exactly as ADR-0008's '(type design)' wording has it, and state for each of the eleven derived facets whether a scored precision record will exist by Step 8 (S-FACET run in Phase 0, with its consumer named per ADR-0012) or the facet is re-scoped out of AC-520's load-time check. Add an S-FACET row to Step 3c's table (registered, unrun; gates any pack row keyed on those facets, per design 10.4) and a Checkpoint 3c grep for it; amend 10.2's Phase-1 Enter column to '(a), (b), (d) and the non-S-BIN half of (c)' or the equivalent; make Step 8 (6, second lint) state its expected branch the way (6) does.

concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) Two things are called 'the corpus'. Design §8.7 (1454) and ADR-0013 place 'the frozen corpus @ 47faec9f' inside redkiln-corpus, and AC-464/AC-444 read 'from the pinned SHA in `redkiln-corpus`'; but RUNBOOK Step 2 copies only PINNED_SHA (spikes/corpus is one file), results, runner, schemas and prompts [measured], while the 1,312-file corpus redkiln-migrate reads and the 360-commit history AC-444 replays live in the predecessor repo at D:/repos/redkiln @ 47faec9f, named in CORPUS_PIN by machine-local path (496). No RUNBOOK step, CI job or ADR fetches it, and 5.2 runs `cargo test --workspace` on a hosted runner: every pinned-corpus fixture test in §13 (AC-440, 444, 451, 452, 459, 460, 461, 469, 479) and AC-440's rk-store test at Step 6 has no input in CI and nothing marks them a local-only suite. Design §0.1's row says 'Yes — `redkiln-migrate` v0 is in Phase 1', yet Checkpoint 7d (2102-2113) never builds or invokes the tool, Step 8's seven checks contain no migration check, AC-463 and the proposal put the differential in Phase 2, and 7d's acceptance set lists AC-440–AC-479 whole [measured]. AC-447 aborts a run producing zero or two commits and AC-450 covers an already-migrated tree, but a kill between writing the new layout and the one commit leaves a target neither AC-440 nor AC-450 describes [measured: 0 hits for dirty/porcelain/interrupt/partial across AC 5470-5760]. The tool must parse YAML frontmatter, fenced ledgers (AC-461) and `.redkiln/processes/*.yaml`, yet design §9.2's fourteen rows, ADR-0084 and Step 7d name no YAML reader — the only survey is the 2026-08-31 RFC (`serde_yaml` archived, `serde_yml` RUSTSEC-2025-0068, `yaml_serde` FINE) [measured]. And AC-460's 'unknown' fixture n is recoverable from s-mig.jsonl: 43 (18/6/19) over its four kinds; its stated reason for excluding plan companions ('dropped by AC-459/AC-479') conflates `plan.md` scaffolds with `_plan.md`, leaving the two `_plan.md` records covered by no criterion [measured]. (ii) F12's 360-commit / 74-slice result was computed by `git log --all` over every ref of the local D:/repos/redkiln clone (118 refs: 42 heads, 41 remote-tracking, 35 tags) [measured]. From the pinned SHA 47faec9f only 46 of 74 slices (8 ever-rejected, not 15) and roughly two-thirds of the trailer commits (231/348 over the Story/Slice-Verdict/Gate keys) are reachable [measured]. F12 itself discloses 'across all refs', but AC-444, AC-464 and design section 5.7 restate the fixture as a read from the pinned SHA via the object store, and the RUNBOOK's redkiln-corpus extraction (RUNBOOK.md:469) copies spikes/corpus, results and runner with no git history: jointly unsatisfiable as written. In the same register AC-006 and AC-188 verify kernel replay 'over corpus logs' from the pinned corpus, which today holds only the old kernel's 124 workflow_run telemetry events (1 of 101 recording the decision field) that a redkiln-rs kernel cannot replay; the golden logs the test needs do not exist and are not marked [WILL EXIST]. An implementer following AC-464 literally reproduces 8/46 and reads the divergence as a reconcile bug; one following AC-188 literally builds a CI test with no valid input.

concerns.title: The three LLM boolean facets have no disposition between Step 4's pre-registered rule and Checkpoint 4a: ADR-0090 as drafted leaves them `source = "llm"` (AC-071 fails closed), and Checkpoint 4a asserts a zero `[true, false]` count, a `surfaces.toml` that exists nowhere and a Halt-8 reading that Step 4a's own instructions cannot satisfy
concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) AC-071's precondition forbids any `source = "llm"` facet until the lint exits 0. RUNBOOK 4.1 (950-951) and 4.5 (1394-1395) pre-register the ADR-0090 decision as 'every ordinal axis is `source = "human"`' — five axes. spikes/p9/facets.toml carries seven `source = "llm"` facets, three of them booleans (`has_repro` 76-78, `external_dep`, `market_facing`) [measured]; ADR-0079:158-165 records a preference for their disposition, not a decision; nineteen catalog/pack rows key on them and 7b's rigor-monotonicity paragraph (1971) presumes `has_repro` remains a live selection input. Checkpoint 4 (1418-1432) has no registry-count line and Checkpoint 4a counts derived facets only. Whoever writes ADR-0090 has no rule for the three, and AC-071 fails closed on them at pack load. (ii) spikes/p9/facets.toml carries eight `values = [true, false]` lines - five derived booleans and three `source = "llm"` booleans (external_dep, market_facing, has_repro) [measured]; 4a.1 scopes the re-shaping to the five, 4a.2 withdraws auth, so following the step leaves three lines, yet Checkpoint 4a asserts zero, and Step 4's decision re-sources ordinal axes only (RUNBOOK:951). ADR-0089 Decision 3 says 'Boolean facets become tri-valued' without a qualifier while its forbids block (line 215) says 'a derived boolean facet', so the count and the checkpoint sit on different readings of the ADR. The same checkpoint tests for a checked-in `surfaces.toml`, which exists nowhere in the tree (ls and git ls-files: 0) [measured], which ADR-0089 makes a per-target-repo artefact, and which 4a defers to S-FACET on the corpus repo; RUNBOOK:1550's 'Six are commands against files that exist today' counts that line among them. Separately, Halt 8 ('a checkpoint you could not run is a failed checkpoint', applies at every step, 'none is discretionary') carries no carve-out for [WILL EXIST] lines although the legend (line 14), Checkpoint 4a's header (1550-1551) and 1569 instruct the deferral, and 1570's expectation 'exit != 0 TODAY' is met by a missing binary - the 'green anyway' shape Halt 8 was written to catch [measured].

concerns.why_before_step5: (i) [inferred] ADR-0090 is the Step-5 gate token and is written at Step 4.4 — before Step 5. Written to 4.1's rule alone it leaves three `llm` facets in the registry that AC-071 fails closed on, or its author improvises an undocumented disposition. Fixed in the pre-registered rule it costs one clause; fixed after ADR-0090 is accepted it needs a successor record. The only concern in this bucket with a pre-Step-5 deadline. (ii) Step 4a runs after Step 4 and before Step 5, and a failed checkpoint is a stop. An implementer will either silently re-shape the three LLM booleans (an edit ADR-0089's forbids block scopes to derived booleans) or seed an empty surfaces.toml in the wrong repository to turn the checkpoint green - the defect golden constraint 7 exists to prevent. Not P0: the fix is a count/scope correction, not a wrong product.
concerns.remediation: (i) Extend RUNBOOK 4.1's pre-registered decision rule with a clause for `has_repro`, `external_dep`, `market_facing` (human-supplied at triage, or dropped per ADR-0079's 'honest destination' option), carry that clause into ADR-0090 when it is written, and add a Checkpoint 4/4a line `grep -c 'source = "llm"' spikes/p9/facets.toml` -> 0 after the edit. (ii) Either extend 4a.3 explicitly to all eight booleans (stating that ADR-0089's tri-valued rule reaches the LLM booleans, or that they are re-sourced to human under Step 4's decision) and keep the zero assertion, or change it to 3 with the three names. Replace the `test -f surfaces.toml` line with an assertion on the corpus/target path S-FACET will seed, or drop it from Checkpoint 4a and move it to S-FACET's own checklist; correct 'Six are commands against files that exist today'. Scope Halt 8: 'lines marked [WILL EXIST] are deferred, not failed; record the deferral and re-run them at the step that builds the path'. Move 1570-1571 into Checkpoint 7b as named re-runs (7b has facet_provenance_fixtures at 1991 but not the lint invocation) with the expectation 'exit != 0 AND stderr names the failing clause' so a missing binary does not pass.

concerns.title: rk-types' closed-output schema rules cannot all hold: 'no `oneOf` anywhere' (ADR-0084:64, RUNBOOK 5.3) vs nested-only (AC-131, design 5.3), the prescribed `#[serde(tag = "kind")]` remedy emits `oneOf` in schemars 1.2.2, the 24/16 caps are documented per-request vendor limits counting union-typed parameters (not house rules, not per-type, not branches-at-a-node), and `StepError` is never enumerated (six variants in step.rs, eleven in the superseded proposal)
concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) Step 5.3 writes `rk-types` and its golden-schema snapshot under two rules that cannot both hold. ADR-0084:64 asserts the exported schema contains 'no `oneOf` anywhere' and :69 prescribes `#[serde(tag = "kind")]` for data-carrying enums 'so they render as a single discriminated object'; design:1742 repeats this tagged [documented, 1P] and Checkpoint 5 greps for zero `oneOf`. [measured] In schemars_derive 1.2.2 `expr_for_internal_tagged_enum` (schema_exprs.rs:347-374) builds one object per variant and calls `variant_subschemas(cont, true, ...)` whose keyword is `if unique { "oneOf" } else { "anyOf" }` (:484); schemas generated with schemars =1.2.2 give oneOf=1 for a `tag = "kind"` enum, anyOf=1 untagged, oneOf=1 externally tagged, `enum` only for a unit enum. So the prescribed shape fails the ADR's own assertion and the checkpoint. The flagship such type, `StepError`, is asserted closed (AC-229) with one event arm per variant (AC-360) but is never enumerated in the governing document: design:1649 says its shape is 'carried from step.rs' (six variants: Transport, Schema, Timeout, Cancelled, NonZero{code,stderr}, UsageLimit) while sections 3.8/7 (:339, :395) name the eleven-variant set of the superseded proposal section 4.3 (Platform, RateLimited, NotAdopted, NotIsolated, Unsupported, Overage, Schema{attempts}, NonZero(143)), which AC-229:2936 cites. The external pass CONFIRMED EXT-CRATEVER-007 on the docs.rs phrase 'generate the schema for the internally tagged ... representation', which does not say 'single object'; the measured schema does not produce one. (ii) AC-131 and design §5.3 row 3 (:665) forbid only a `oneOf`/`anyOf` nested inside another; ADR-0084:64, design §9.5 (:1744) and RUNBOOK 5.3 (:1741, :1762) forbid any `oneOf` at any node and are silent on `anyOf`. Under the stronger rule AC-131's nested-union must-fail fixture and AC-157's 17-branch fixture fail for the wrong reason (no union node may exist), so the two lints are vacuous. AC-157 caps 'union branches at any node' and discloses abandoning the '≤16 union fields' reading; RUNBOOK:1742 and ADR-0084 keep '≤ 16 union fields per type' — the same test phrased as two counts [measured]. Checkpoint 5 greps `oneOf` only; schemars_derive emits `anyOf` for `#[serde(untagged)]` [measured], which passes the checkpoint while violating the no-union intent. The stricter rule wins in practice because Checkpoint 5 sits in the same step, so Step 5 does not build the wrong thing; the register, RUNBOOK and ADR disagree on what the snapshot test asserts. (iii) The corpus states in four live places that the vendor's structured-outputs page carries no limits table and that the <=24 optional / <=16 union caps are this project's own budget which 'must not be presented as documented vendor limits'. The page carries an explicit 'Schema complexity limits' table today and, per a Wayback capture of 2026-09-07, carried it before the corpus's 2026-09-08 read, so the 'no limits table' sentence was a truncation artefact, not a vendor change [documented]. The vendor's caps differ from the corpus's in two ways that bear on Step 5.3: they are totals per REQUEST across all strict tool schemas plus the JSON output schema (with a further 20-strict-tools-per-request cap and a 180 s compile timeout), and the 16 counts 'parameters that use anyOf or type arrays', not union branches at a node, which is the quantity AC-157 and the snapshot lint check. A schemars Option<T> field renders as a type array, so a type passing AC-132 with 24 optional fields could carry 24 union-typed parameters and breach the vendor's 16 while every corpus lint is green [inferred]; F20 records that closed-output violations fail open at exit 0, so the breach would be silent. Self-flagged UNVERIFIED in the corpus; first verification fails.

concerns.why_before_step5: (i) Step 5.3 builds rk-types and the snapshot test. Any data-carrying enum written to ADR-0084's remedy fails Checkpoint 5 with no corpus guidance on which rule gives, and the kernel (7b) and adapter (7c) will match exhaustively against whichever StepError set the 5.3 author picks -- six copied from step.rs or eleven reconstructed from a superseded document. P1 not P0: the workstream is specific (schema export, AC-129-133; StepError, AC-229/AC-360) and one record before 5.3 fences it. (ii) Step 5 writes this exact test (RUNBOOK:1700 cites AC-129–133/157/158 as what the snapshot enforces). Implementer A ships AC-131's nesting lint plus AC-157's per-node branch count and allows a top-level `oneOf`; implementer B ships the RUNBOOK grep and a per-type union-field count. A fails Checkpoint 5; B has no instrument for AC-131's must-fail fixture. The set of legal Rust enum shapes differs between them. (iii) Step 5.3 writes the golden-schema snapshot test with the caps as per-type house rules and instructs 'Do not cite them as a platform constraint'. Built as written, the lint counts branches-at-a-node where the vendor counts union-typed parameters, and it counts per type where the vendor counts per request; the rk-types authoring budget and its fixtures (25-optional, 17-branch) would be committed against the wrong constraint, and a vendor breach fails open (F20). concerns.remediation: (i) One record before Step 5.3: (a) supersede ADR-0084's schema clause (never edit) -- either adopt AC-131's rule (no nested oneOf/anyOf plus the branch cap) and change the Checkpoint 5 grep to detect nesting, or keep 'no oneOf anywhere' and state the true constraint: no multi-variant data-carrying enum in any exported type, flattened to a struct with a unit `kind` enum plus optional payload fields (which spends the <=24 optional budget); (b) in the same record or an amendment to the harness area file, one table listing every `StepError` variant, its payload, its retry class (AC-029/AC-234), whether `spoke()` is true, and its event arm; (c) correct design:1649 to 'the `spoke()` predicate and raw-retention pattern carry from step.rs; the variant set is redesigned', and drop design:1742's [documented, 1P] tag for the single-object claim. (ii) State one rule identically in AC-131, AC-157, design §5.3 and RUNBOOK 5.3 — recommended: 'no `oneOf` at any node (data-carrying enums use `#[serde(tag = "kind")]`); `anyOf` permitted only as schemars' nullable-Option form, never nested; ≤16 branches per `anyOf`/`enum` node'. Restore 'branches at any node' at RUNBOOK:1742. Extend Checkpoint 5 to `grep -rnE 'oneOf|anyOf'` with the nesting check in the test itself. ADR-0084 is accepted: leave it and let the AC carry the precise form, or supersede it if the 'anywhere' rule is being relaxed. (iii) (1) RUNBOOK §5.3 (:1740-1744) and architecture-design :666/:2009 by dated amendment: cite the vendor's 'Schema complexity limits' table (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs, fetched 2026-09-10) as the source of 24/16, state the per-request scope (all strict tool schemas plus the JSON output schema; 20 strict tools; 180 s compile), and delete 'Do not cite them as a platform constraint'. (2) ADR-0084 :117 is an accepted record: issue a short successor record correcting the evidence line; do not edit 0084. (3) Re-specify AC-157 (and the snapshot assertion) to count union-typed parameters - any property whose schema uses anyOf or a type array, nullable Option<T> included - per exported schema, retaining the 17-parameter fixture; keep AC-132 as is. (4) State the precondition under which per-type equals per-request - one output schema per dispatch and no strict user-defined tools on the command line - as a GIVEN in AC-132/AC-157 and as a lint on the adapter's argv, so that adding a strict tool later re-opens the budget. (5) Register S-SCHEMA-CAP (consumer: rk-types snapshot test, AC-132/AC-157, AC-129 fail-open guard): submit a 17-union-parameter schema and a 25-optional schema to the pinned CLI and record the observed failure shape, because F20 says the failure is silent and nothing in the corpus has observed the vendor's rejection.

concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) ADR-0086 places the memoisation table in the EventStore (SQLite, the tier-2 substrate) [documented], while AC-161 requires the next action to survive deleting that file and AC-187 requires a committed mid-graph step to resolve by memo key rather than re-dispatch; the design's tier-1 list (stage transitions, gates, verdicts, seals) names no step result or memo entry, ADR-0087:46 serialises bound step outputs 'to disk' with no substrate, and F38's mid-graph state lived under spikes/results/p8-state/, a directory the design never maps, so the tier annotation AC-160 demands at compile time has no answer [measured]. The same record carries two further inconsistencies: the key is five components in AC-014/AC-019 but the schema's step key has seven and ADR-0021/AC-017 add the loop iteration counter, so AC-019's 'five components' field set cannot carry what AC-017 requires (AC-014's five miss-cases still pass against the wider key; only AC-019 is unsatisfiable) [measured]; and ADR-0021's forbids block still requires `memo = false` on live-state tool steps while ADR-0059's forbids block makes that declaration illegal, the partial supersession living only in 0021's Evidence prose with `superseded_by: []`, 0059 superseding 0043 alone, 0059 listed as `related`, and README:159 counting nine links where its own rule gives ten [measured]. The corpus records the tier judgement as unsettled and the clause's withdrawal; it does not record that AC-161 and AC-187 cannot both hold under ADR-0086's placement, nor the key-count or frontmatter defects. (ii) ADR-0059 (accepted; supersedes ADR-0043 and partially ADR-0021) moves liveness to `live = true` on the verb's registry entry and its forbids block bars a step from declaring `memo = false` as its own liveness assertion. AC-018 (in Step 7b's AC-001–AC-039 acceptance set, RUNBOOK:2006) and design §3.5:325 still prescribe exactly that per-step declaration, list only ADR-0021/ADR-0064 as decisions, and the register's ADR table (AC:6485) maps ADR-0059 to AC-070/072/520 only [measured]. The design records the withdrawal at :324, one row above the row that ignores it. The lint rule and must-fail fixture AC-018 prescribes are the thing ADR-0059's forbids block bars, so one rk-kernel pack-lint workstream builds against an accepted ADR. (iii) AC-010/011/012, AC-508 and design:306/320 key each dispatch by `(run_id, activity_id, attempt)`; activity-graph-schema.md:10 keys it by `(run_id, activity_id, step_id, attempt)` while citing proposal section 4.2, which states the three-part key -- the schema added `step_id` while claiming to restate the proposal [measured]. Under ADR-0022 each agent/tool step is its own dispatch with its own `retry = { max = N }` (schema:83), so AC-011's log-wide uniqueness and AC-012's one-`activity_committed`-per-`(run_id, activity_id)` cannot both hold for a multi-step activity, and no text says at which granularity `attempt` increments. The memo key is five components at design:322/AC-014/AC-019, a per-step key with an iteration counter at AC-017/ADR-0021:26, a different list again at schema:87 (activity id@version, rigor, step id, resolved input digests, card digest or toolchain version + command, injected KB atoms), a four-tuple at design:1014 and a three-tuple at AC-336 [measured]; no document names the hash framing (length-prefixed vs concatenated), the canonicalisation of `resolved inputs`, what 'toolchain version' denotes (the Toolchain port's `detect()`, AC-226's pinned CLI version, or the redkiln binary), or the output `schema_version`, so a schema migration (AC-135) hits the memo and fails AC-136's read instead of missing, and `memo_hit`'s journalled field set is undefined.

concerns.title: The Harness port's `dispatch`/`cancel(handle)` contract is unimplementable as written: blocking dispatch, a handle no caller can hold, no slot for the AC-360 record, no `Send`/`Sync` bounds or trait-object shape, a POSIX process-group cancel that never holds on Windows (the lifted runner does `taskkill /T /F`; AC-225's 'exits 143' never obtains), and an S-BIN-blocked `ChangeSummary` placeholder with no stated home
concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) The design sketches the harness port as a sync `dispatch(ActivitySpec) -> Result<Typed, StepError>` plus `cancel(handle)`, and ADR-0076 requires the handle to be 'minted when the operation started' while its Decision has the sync method block on the adapter's runtime until the child exits; no caller can therefore hold the handle before `dispatch` returns, and no text names who calls cancel (a Ctrl-C handler, a wall-clock watchdog, a second thread) or from which thread [measured]. `Result<Typed, StepError>` has no slot for the usage/headroom/effective-config record AC-360 requires on every termination path, whereas the runner the adapter lifts returns `(StepRecord, Result<..>)` [measured]. `ActivitySpec`, `Typed` and the handle type are never given fields, and `Typed` cannot be a per-call generic on an object-safe trait under AC-480 [inferred]. The spike runner carries only the timeout kill (runner.rs:356-359); its `Cancelled` variant is `dead_code` (step.rs:190) [measured]. (ii) Design:266 gives `dispatch` a completed-value return and ADR-0076 makes every port method block the calling thread with the kernel never observing interleaving, so a cancel handle 'minted when the operation started' cannot reach the kernel until `dispatch` returns, and no text names who calls `cancel` (composition root, CLI signal path) or whether Toolchain/DocsSite carry one [measured: grep of design, AC register, RUNBOOK and ADR-0076]; nothing states whether the five traits carry `Send + Sync` or whether the kernel holds `Box<dyn Port>` or `Arc<dyn Port + Send + Sync>`, though ADR-0076:56 sends fan-out to threads. Design:269 gives the Toolchain port `change_summary(range) -> ChangeSummary` and AC-497, inside 7a's AC-480..AC-519 set, asserts 'a typed `ChangeSummary` value', while Checkpoint 5 greps only `crates/rk-types/src` for the S-BIN-blocked name and Checkpoint 8 forbids a finalised type; RUNBOOK 7a never mentions the method [measured: every RUNBOOK `ChangeSummary` line is a prohibition], so the placeholder's home and the Phase-1 return type are unstated and both fences are satisfiable by a placeholder anywhere else. Checkpoint 7c builds `rk-adapter-node`, a name that occurs once in the corpus; design section 9.1 and the proposal name `rk-adapter-toolchain-node`, and the AC register's owner labels include eight names (`rk-port-toolchain` 5 rows, `rk-kernel-verify` 30, `rk-select` 23, `rk-catalog` 18, `rk-packs` 12, `rk-store-artifacts`, `rk-policy`, `rk-doctor`) that are not section 9.1 crate families, with no sentence saying the label is a subject tag [measured]. (iii) AC-224, ADR-0076's Decision and design section 3.8.2 specify the adapter's cancel as a POSIX 'process-group kill'. The corpus knows Windows needs a Job Object (SM-068:528; AC-278 verified-by :3097; the note at :3537) but says so only for AC-278/SM-068, never for AC-224, and the runner that section 9.1 says 'survives unchanged' inside `rk-adapter-claude` does neither: on Windows it runs `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` (a parent-tree walk that needs the parent alive and misses re-parented grandchildren, the F22 survivor shape) and elsewhere `child.kill()`, which reaches only the direct child (runner.rs:469-481) [measured]. AC-225's GIVEN/WHEN ('exits 143') is SIGTERM semantics that never obtains on Windows: a `taskkill /F` victim exits 1 [measured, this audit, Windows 11]; the AC's own negative test already implies keying the classifier on 'cancel was issued', so the WHEN clause disagrees with its own instrument. A Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE needs FFI under the workspace-wide `unsafe_code = "deny"`; ADR-0083:68 already licenses the one commented override, so the only gap is that nothing names it for this crate.

concerns.title: ADR-0088 misnames its source paper and inverts its mechanism: under bug-free framing false positives collapse, they do not 'barely move'
concerns.statement: ADR-0088 adds a 'confirmation-bias arm' to S-SUBTLE on the authority of arXiv 2603.18740, which it cites as 'Measuring and Exploiting Confirmation Bias in LLM-Assisted Security Code Review' and characterises as finding that bug-free framing cuts detection 'by 16-93%' with an effect 'strongly asymmetric: false negatives rise sharply while false positives barely move'. The corpus records that the full paper was not read. Read in full on 2026-09-10: the title is 'Contextual Bias', the phrase 'confirmation bias' never appears; the 16-93 band is percentage points, under the STRONG bug-free condition only, on 5 of 6 models, and the omitted sixth (Claude Opus 4.5) drops 4.9 pp, not significant; and the asymmetry runs the other way. Under strong bug-free framing the 'Fixed' rate on patched code rises +46 to +95 pp, so false positives collapse alongside detection; it is bug-PRESENT framing that barely moves anything, because false-positive rates are already above 88% at neutral (a ceiling). The decision (add a prior-approval arm, report FN separately) survives because detection does drop, but the symmetric 'presented as already rejected' arm was rejected partly on 'the source finds false positives barely move under framing manipulation', which the source contradicts, and the arm's name, the ADR title and the design's §10.4 register all inherit the misnomer. [documented]

anchors.quote: framing a change as "bug-free" before review reduces the vulnerability-detection rate by 16–93%**, and that the effect is **strongly asymmetric: false negatives rise sharply while false positives barely move**.

Rejected on the measured asymmetry and on cost: the source finds false positives barely move under framing manipulation, the over-rejection direction is already covered by Jin & Chen and answered by the re-execution rule

*Measuring and Exploiting Confirmation Bias in LLM-Assisted Security Code Review* (~Mar 2026, arXiv 2603.18740): a controlled experiment over 250 CVE vulnerability–patch pairs finds that framing a change as "bug-free" before review reduces the vulnerability-detection rate by **16–93%**

concerns.title: ADR-0079's external corroboration overstates three preprints: the schema-induced mechanism, P1-BOUND's boundary premise, Essence Coach
concerns.statement: Three external corroborations of F36's instability finding say more than their sources. (1) architecture-design:143's joint summary, 'corroborated across five 2026 frontier models, with Claude-Sonnet-4 measured at background temperature 0 - the instability is schema-induced, not decoding noise [preprint, arXiv 2603.04417; arXiv 2604.22411]', attaches a mechanism neither paper states: 2603.04417 tests Claude-Sonnet-4.5 (not Sonnet-4, which is 2604.22411's), finds Anthropic models 'often show minimal reductions and, in some cases, increased variability at temperature 0', and attributes this to 'deeper architectural or decoding-level differences' [documented]. The per-source rows (:2030, evidence-augmentation:200, ADR-0079:222) are exact; the mechanism clause is ADR-0079's own inference presented as external. (2) 'reports classification instability correlating with proximity to the decision boundary' (architecture-design:457, :1839, :2032; evidence-augmentation:202; ADR-0079:231) credits arXiv 2511.01176 with a finding it does not measure: the boundary sentence is an unmeasured premise in its section 5.2, and its measured result is consistency over five identical submissions with temperature having 'a small influence' [documented]. P1-BOUND, the registered diagnostic, rests on that premise. (3) evidence-augmentation:99 and ADR-0079:140 credit arXiv 2508.16445 ('Essence Coach') with flagging that 'Essence assessment requires precise criterion matching probabilistic models struggle to guarantee'; three full-text passes over v1 and v2 find no such statement, the paper's stated limitations being dataset size, no comparison and manual validation; v2 (2026-09-01) is retitled 'Essence Coach: A Bot for Software Practice Adoption' [documented]. The decisions survive on other grounds: the temperature-arm prohibition is licensed by 04417's own T=0 result for Anthropic models and by 2511.01176's small temperature effect; P1-BOUND is desk work over existing draws and costs nothing. What changes is the tag and the wording.

concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) Two [documented]/[1P] attributions in ADR-0083 and its design and evidence-augmentation restatements are not in the cited sources. (1) 'nursery lints can change or be removed without notice' (ADR-0083:29, :67, :117; architecture-design:1720; evidence-augmentation:149) appears in no Clippy text: the Lints book says the nursery group 'contains lints which are buggy or need more work' and 'It is not recommended to enable the whole group', the README says 'new lints that are still under development'; and 'false-positive-prone' is the book's description of pedantic, not nursery [documented]. (2) 'the "pin for a binary you control" framing is the blog's' (ADR-0083:118; architecture-design:1718; evidence-augmentation:150) attributes to swatinem.de a framing the post does not contain: it never mentions `package.rust-version`, floors, libraries or binaries, and the corpus never read it (evidence-augmentation:401 'URL not returned'); the application framing is RFC 3537's ('an application with a vetted toolchain') [documented]. Neither decision changes: nursery at warn is licensed by 'not recommended to enable the whole group', and the pin by RFC 3537 alone. The `clippy::correctness`-only-deny and `clippy::cargo`-is-manifest halves of :117 are exact. (ii) ADR-0083 and RUNBOOK 5.1 justify `clippy::nursery = "warn"` as a whole group 'on the documented grounds that nursery lints can change or be removed without notice' and tag the sentence [1P] Clippy Lints book. The book contains no such sentence. Its nursery text is 'lints which are buggy or need more work. It is **not** recommended to enable the whole group, but rather cherry-pick lints', so enabling the group at warn is the thing the source advises against, and the ADR's n=1 first-party citation supports a claim the source does not make. The ADR also reserves per-crate `#![allow]`/`#![deny]` 'as a visible, commented override'; `#[expect(lint, reason = "...")]` has been stable since 1.81 and is the self-cleaning form (a stale expectation is itself a lint), which Microsoft's M-STATIC-VERIFICATION uses. The enumerated-pedantic-subset choice is a legitimate stricter variant of Microsoft's warn-group-with-opt-outs and needs no change. [documented] (iii) First verification of four self-flagged sources shows the evidence sections of two accepted convention ADRs inverted or overstated what their sources say [documented]. ADR-0083 :118: 'The "pin for a binary you control" framing is the blog's, corroborated by RFC 3537' - swatinem.de recommends pinning as 'yet another dependency' and never mentions rust-version, floors, libraries or binaries (zero grep hits); the application-vs-library, pin-vs-floor framing is RFC 3537's own text, so the attribution is backwards. ADR-0085 :108: 'MADR's own bare/minimal cut keeps title, Context and Problem Statement, Decision Outcome and status/date only' - the minimal template keeps Considered Options (mandatory per the 4.0.0 CHANGELOG), optional Consequences, and has no frontmatter at all. ADR-0085 :29/:109 and adr/README.md :13: MADR 'permits Consequences/Confirmation to be updated over time' - not in MADR's template, CHANGELOG or docs; inference tagged [documented]. ADR-0085 :108 and evidence-augmentation :231: 'adr-tools and Log4brains regenerate a README/index table from frontmatter on each new record' - Log4brains rejects NNNN numbering by design (YYYYMMDD-slug.md), infers metadata from raw text and git log, and adr-tools regenerates a TOC only on an explicit `adr generate toc`. Every decision (exact pin; immutability as this repo's chosen convention; generate-don't-hand-maintain) survives.

concerns.title: ADR-0083:68 prescribes a per-crate manifest `[lints]` override that Cargo rejects beside `workspace = true`; :70 names the working route
concerns.statement: ADR-0083:63 requires every member to carry `[lints] workspace = true` 'and nothing else'; ADR-0083:68 then says a crate that needs `unsafe_code` 'overrides in its own manifest's `[lints]`'. Cargo does not allow both: RFC 3389 makes any other key beside `workspace = true` in `[lints]` a hard error, and rust-lang/cargo #13157 ('cannot override workspace.lints in lints'), which the ADR cites as support, is the open issue asking for exactly the override :68 prescribes [documented]. The route that works is the one :70 already permits, a commented `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` source attribute 'for something the manifest cannot express', and RUNBOOK:1649-1650 is consistent with it. The evidence ledger also cites the wrong Cargo Book page: /cargo/reference/lints.html documents Cargo's own lints and shows only `[workspace.lints.cargo]`; the `[workspace.lints.rust]` / `[lints] workspace = true` mechanism is on the Workspaces and Manifest pages [documented]. The lint policy itself is unaffected.

anchors.quote: **Lints.** `[workspace.lints.rust]` and `[workspace.lints.clippy]` live in the root manifest; every member crate carries `[lints] workspace = true` and nothing else. Within that table:

- `unsafe_code = "deny"` at the workspace level. A crate that genuinely needs it overrides in its own manifest's `[lints]` with a comment naming why — the point of the workspace table is that the exception is then the only thing that looks different.
A per-crate `#![allow]`/`#![deny]` in source is permitted only as a visible, commented override for something the manifest cannot express, and never as a way to restate workspace policy.
Cargo Book, Lints — https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/lints.html (with rust-lang/cargo #13157) ·

concerns.title: Omitting `package.rust-version` leaves the edition-2024 MSRV-aware resolver inert; the ADR rejected substitution, not co-existence
concerns.statement: ADR-0083 pins an exact rustc in rust-toolchain.toml and says 'package.rust-version is not used as a substitute' because 'a floor tells a consumer the minimum version ... Nobody consumes these crates'. Cargo treats the two as complementary, not alternatives: edition 2024 selects resolver 3, which changes `resolver.incompatible-rust-versions` from allow to fallback, and that fallback 'will prefer packages with a Rust version that is less than or equal to your own Rust version' only when `rust-version` is set; `cargo add` likewise selects a dependency version compatible with the declared rust-version. With the pin at 1.97.1 and no rust-version, a dependency whose latest release requires a newer rustc is resolved anyway and breaks the pinned build, which is the CI outage the pin exists to prevent. Microsoft M-MSRV says an MSRV should be set when crates are first created. The ADR's rejection was aimed at substitution and is correct; the floor set equal to the pin is what makes the edition-2024 resolver do its job. [documented]

anchors.quote: Rejected: a floor tells a *consumer* the minimum version that will compile the crate. Nobody consumes these crates. The question here is "which rustc built this binary", and only the pin answers it.
`package.rust-version` is not used as a substitute.
The "pin for a binary you control" framing is the blog's, corroborated by RFC 3537's separate treatment of the floor — it is not a first-party recommendation for this project shape.
A pin and a floor answer different questions and are not substitutes. `package.rust-version` is not a substitute

Add the line to RUNBOOK 5.1's `[workspace.package]` block. Owner: Step 5 workspace author.

concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) (1) Phase-1 exit check (3) is `redkiln run --resume <run-id>` (RUNBOOK:2155, the only `--resume` in the runbook). Design :321/:1267/:1278, AC-013, AC-186 ('no `--resume`, `--continue` or equivalent flag exists on any command'), AC-264 and AC-400 all deny the flag; AC-264's Verified-by asserts that exact invocation exits as an unknown argument and AC-400's router lint fails the build on the name. The same block uses `run --lane fix --item` and `explain --run <run-id> --stages`, shapes found nowhere else in the corpus [measured]. (2) AC-001's Verified-by and exit check (4) (RUNBOOK:1952, :2160) run clippy with `-D warnings`, which promotes every nursery lint to an error — the group deny ADR-0083:106 forbids and whose CI-outage rationale RUNBOOK:1638–1640 states; measured on the RUNBOOK manifest, `missing_const_for_fn` became 'error … implied by -D warnings'. As written, `cargo clippy --workspace -D warnings` is rejected by cargo ('unexpected argument -D'), so exit check (4) cannot run. (3) ADR-0084:58 pins gix 'in the workspace dependency table'; Checkpoint 6 (RUNBOOK:1850) greps `crates/rk-git/Cargo.toml` for the literal `gix = "=0.87.1"`, which returns 0 for the ADR-conformant `gix.workspace = true` [measured]. The build is fenced three ways against (1), and (2)/(3) are one-line command fixes; no workstream is blocked. (ii) RUNBOOK Step 8's exit criterion (3), the third of 'seven runnable checks', is written as `./target/debug/redkiln run --resume <run-id>` - the only `--resume` invocation in the corpus [measured, grep] - while AC-400 (in Step 7d's own acceptance set) places `--resume` on the committed denylist with a build-failing router lint, AC-186 and AC-264 say no such flag exists, AC-013 gives `redkiln run <item>` as the re-entry, and design lines 321/731/773/1267 say 'no --resume, --continue or equivalent flag exists on any command'. The command also addresses the run by `<run-id>` where every other anchor takes an item, and RUNBOOK:2134 itself invokes `run --lane fix --item`; lines 2149-2157 carry no qualifier. As written, exit check (3) cannot pass on a binary that satisfies AC-400: an operator following it literally records a false failure or adds the forbidden flag and breaks AC-400's snapshot test. Three finders reported it independently; the refuters corrected it P1 to P2 because AC-400's lint fences the flag and the fix is one line - the highest-value P2 in this bucket.

anchors.quote: ./target/debug/redkiln run --resume <run-id>
WHEN `redkiln run <item>` re-enters (there is no `--resume` flag)
WHEN any invocation passes a flag whose name appears on the committed resume-shaped denylist (`--resume`, `--continue`,
`redkiln run` refuses a resume-shaped flag by a **committed name denylist** (`--resume`, `--continue`, `--retry-step`,
THEN the invocation is refused as an unknown argument, and no denylisted name appears anywhere in the snapshot.
- Forbids denying `clippy::pedantic` or `clippy::nursery` as groups.

Step 8 is the bar every Phase-1 step is built toward, and 7d's CLI author reads Step 8 for the command surface the exit needs; the correct form must be written before the CLI snapshot is committed in 7d.
concerns.remediation: (i) (1) Rewrite RUNBOOK:2155 as `taskkill /T /F …` then `./target/debug/redkiln run <item>` (same item, run_id read back from the event log per AC-013), asserting digest equality via `explain <item>`; align checks (1)–(2) of the same block with the §8 verb table or extend the table and AC-400's snapshot deliberately. (2) Amend AC-001's Verified-by and RUNBOOK:1952/:2160 to `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` gated on exit code, and reword Checkpoint 5 (:1755) to 'exit 0; nursery warnings permitted'; if warnings-as-errors is wanted, set nursery to allow by superseding ADR-0083. (3) Change Checkpoint 6 to `grep -c 'gix = "=0.87.1"' Cargo.toml` → 1 and `grep -c 'gix.workspace = true' crates/rk-git/Cargo.toml` → 1. (ii) Amend RUNBOOK:2155 to `./target/debug/redkiln run --lane fix --item <item>` re-invoked after the kill (the idempotent re-entry, AC-013), keeping the digest-equality assertion unchanged and taking any run id for the `explain` comparison from `redkiln explain --run` as criterion (1) does; add a one-line note that `--resume` being refused is itself AC-400's/AC-264's behavioural check. No ADR change.

concerns.title: rk-store and redkiln-migrate contracts: locator end rule, Gwt shape, conservation vocabulary, and no locator/carrier/predicate for three criteria
concerns.statement: The locator is 'a heading-anchored slice' and nothing in the proposal, ADR-0005/0006, design section 5.1 or AC-149..AC-151 says where a slice ends or what a 'genuine heading' is, so AC-152 (accept headings inside prose) and AC-151 (error on a duplicate genuine heading) collide and AC-150's decoys cover neither a deeper heading inside a slice nor a same-level duplicate in prose [measured: 'next heading', 'same level', 'sentinel', 'end of section' occur 0 times]. `Gwt` is `Option<Gwt>` in six documents and defined in none; S-MIG detected GWT by substring inside the `criterion` cell (census-s-mig.py:165), no document says whether migration populates `gwt`/`verification` (0 hits), and AC-454's 'both fields absent' property over the 19 affected specs is either false (they hold 208 ACs, 77 with both fields, 29 lacking both) or trivially true [measured, uncapped rerun]. AC-451 names five conservation buckets, SM-134 four, design:1467 five, and the census whose N=6,877 they must reproduce partitions into seven (Opaque 3,513 / Lifted 3,011 / EmptyTemplate 112 / Unmapped 81 / LiftedWithLoss 73 / Failed 54 / Missing 33) with no mapping for the 33 Missing, 63 section-level Unmapped or 2 non-plan EmptyTemplate records, so one implementer folds Missing into failed (contradicting AC-453's per-slot counts) and another never balances N [measured, s-mig.jsonl]. AC-475's 'change/diff material' has no locator -- at the pin one .bklg file carries diff hunks and 156 '## Changes' sections that S-MIG's settled opaque list already routes to opaque with no marker -- and its loss marker presupposes a typed `ChangeSummary` slot S-BIN has not designed; AC-461's 'fix recorded as an enumerated manual intervention' names no carrier for the fixed bytes (a corpus SHA bump is closed by ADR-0013, AC-464 and the frozen pin, so the carrier must live in the migrate crate) and AC-449/AC-467 do not list it among the determinism inputs; AC-440's typed unsupported-layout error names no recognition predicate and AC-442's one-crate allowlist no detector [measured].

anchors.quote: The one piece of markdown logic that survives is a **section locator** for the opaque prose fields — a heading-anchored slice, not a grammar — and it is tested as such.
GIVEN a document in which the target anchor occurs zero times, or more than once as a genuine heading
| 1 | The AC type is `{ id, criterion: text, gwt: Option<Gwt>, verification: Option<text> }` — permissive by construction |
write → read → validate with both fields absent; a `jsonschema` conformance test asserting `gwt` and `verification`
THEN the report accounts for exactly N records as lifted + lifted-with-loss + failed + opaque + dropped-by-decision
GIVEN historical change/diff material in the corpus and no settled `ChangeSummary` type

concerns.why_before_step5: Step 5 ships `rk-types::AcceptanceCriterion` (RUNBOOK 5.3 lists Spec among its types) and names AC-475 in its acceptance set (RUNBOOK:1717) -- defining `Gwt` is a small decision the implementer can take and record, so P2 not P1. Step 6's rk-store locator is the one piece of markdown logic in the system and the thing SM-043 measures from first use with no baseline; the migrate crate's report schema (AC-448) and conservation assert are its first definitions. Each reading builds, but AC-150's byte ranges, AC-454's property, AC-451's identity and AC-475's fixture cannot be authored identically by two implementers.
concerns.remediation: Design section 5.1 row 4 and AC-149 (dated amendment): 'an anchor is a heading at the template's declared level for that section; the slice runs from the line after the anchor to the next heading at that level or shallower, or end of file; deeper headings inside the slice are prose bytes and not anchors', with an AC-150 deeper-heading decoy and an AC-151 same-level-duplicate-in-prose fixture. Design section 5.2 row 1: define `Gwt { given: Text, when: Text, then: Text, and: Vec<Text> }` (or state that gwt is a presence flag), add to ADR-0075's amendment note and AC-137 that migration never populates `gwt` or `verification` from criterion text -- both are authored fields from the first CLI write -- and rewrite AC-454 as 'over all 153 specs at the pin, every AC round-trips byte-identical with both fields absent'. AC-451 and SM-134: enumerate the report's outcome vocabulary (lifted, with-loss, failed, opaque, unmapped-section, missing-expected, empty-template, dropped-by-decision) with the mapping from census outcomes and per-bucket N at the pin from s-mig.jsonl. AC-475: name the locator (which sections and files count as change material at the pin, with the measured counts) and its SM-134 bucket (opaque vs with_loss), keeping the tripwire conjunct. AC-461: name the carrier (`interventions.toml` in the migrate crate: path, line, reason, replacement bytes, digest of the original) and add it to AC-449's determinism inputs and AC-467's versioned lifter set. AC-440: state the predicate (absence of the new-layout manifest plus presence of `.bklg/`) and allowlist that one detector explicitly in AC-442.

concerns.title: Checkpoint 5's snapshot guard fails for the ADR-0083 test layout, and no RUNBOOK line accepts the initial insta snapshots
concerns.statement: insta stores snapshots in a `snapshots` directory beside the file containing the assertion. Under ADR-0083's mandated `tests/it/main.rs` layout they land at `crates/rk-types/tests/it/snapshots/`, so Checkpoint 5's `test -d crates/rk-types/tests/snapshots` guard -- added to stop a false pass -- fails deterministically for the conformant implementer and passes only for the one-file-per-case layout the ADR rejects [measured: reproduced with insta 1.48.0; first `cargo test` exits 101 with 'stored new snapshot ...tests/it/snapshots/it__schema__schema_snapshot.snap.new']. The RUNBOOK installs cargo-insta (1688) and names `cargo insta accept` only as a rubber-stamp hazard (1745); on a first run insta writes `.snap.new` and the assertion fails, so `cargo test --workspace # exit 0` cannot hold until an accept that no line instructs. Both halves are Checkpoint 5 lines: the first checkpoint of the first product crate fails twice for an implementer who follows the ADR.

anchors.quote: test -d crates/rk-types/tests/snapshots \
at most one integration-test binary per crate under test, structured as `tests/it/main.rs` with `mod` declarations for the cases — never one file per case.
cargo install cargo-insta --locked

concerns.title: The design diverges from the binding register it defers to: AC-511 is 'unresolved' in five design lines the register settles (and the register re-issued six cut ids against ADR-0085 rule 7); AC-356's withdrawn AND clause is still criterion text; the design says `schema_version` where AC-111/AC-117 and ADR-0072 say `version`; thirteen never-committed `ac-*.md` area files are named as owners; and reconcile.rs sits in opposite states on each side
concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) reconcile.rs: design 0.1 row 55, 1.3:184, 5:252, 9.1:1653 and ADR-0002:52 say it was 'rewritten in the spike and validated on 360 commits / 74 slices'; the AC register (:2468-2471, :4514) and SM-051 cut that as 'fabricated' with 'no spike in the brief that built or validated a reconcile.rs'; ground truth is spikes/runner/src/reconcile.rs (420 lines, tracked, 330d46c 'S0.2 RESULT'), which produced F12, whose limits say it reconstructed state over the corpus but was NOT validated against agent decisions (n=1) - so the design overclaims 'validated', the register overcorrects to 'not built', RUNBOOK Step 2 deletes spikes/runner before Step 6, and Step 6 never says where rk-git's sanctioned import (AC-443) is lifted from [measured]. AC-356: design:1025 withdraws the binary-class mutation exemption ('a design sketch under a block, not a relaxation') and RUNBOOK:1723 keeps the per-AC norm in force, but the register's AND clause (:4381) still states it as criterion text, its PROVISIONAL note covering only field names, and as worded it makes 'asset touched + test/capture result' sufficient evidence, which ADR-0019's forbids block rules out [documented]. AC-511: the register's 0.4, 0.3 and ports-dist area key settle it as the `--bare` half split from AC-488 (AC-513 retired), while the design's 8.8 row and 10.x note say the conflict is 'carried rather than resolved' and 'the sources do not settle which criterion holds the id', and design:362 places it in cli-doctor where the register places it in ports-dist [measured]. `version`: design:534 and :1333 attribute to AC-111/AC-117 and ADR-0072 a rule that a shipped activity's coherence edit bumps `schema_version`, but the cited rows (AC:1590, :1599), ADR-0072 (:43, :48, :54) and schema S9c.42 name the activity's `version` field; `schema_version` is the per-artifact-type field (design:669, AC-135, AC:5858), which the register itself separates at :1812-1813 [measured]. (ii) [measured] The register's §0.4 (:122) and AC-511's own body (:6069, 'Uses the id freed by the cut of the old AC-511') settle AC-511 as the `--bare` half split from AC-488, so the design's §8.4 and §2 citations of it are correct; but design :357, :362, :1345, :1585 and :1969 still say 'the sources do not settle which criterion holds the id' and tell the builder to re-read the area file before touching either statement — for a question the binding register already answers. What no record licenses: the register re-issued AC-511, AC-512 and four other ids after cutting them, which ADR-0085 rule 7 ('Ids are never reused within their scope') and its forbids block ('forbids reusing a retired number') prohibit; §0.4 distinguishes 'cut and freed' from 'retired' on its own authority. If cut ids may be re-issued, every pre-refutation citation of one of the six is suspect — the hazard §0.4 itself warns of. (iii) [measured] `git ls-files` and `git log --all --name-only` return no `ac-*.md` path: the thirteen area files the register says it was 'assembled from' (AC :6532) never entered the repository. The design nonetheless names an `ac-<area>.md` file on seven lines (:511, :682, :1178, :1333, :1847, :1900, :1961) with section labels (§1c, §1.2, §1.7) that resolve nowhere (the register homes are §4.3, §11.2, §6.7), states at :349 and :1968 that 'the area file owns the wording', and at :362 instructs that AC-218 and AC-428 'must be reconciled in the area files before either is built'; no sentence discloses the files as uncommitted scratch. In the 60-id seeded mirror diff the one divergence between the design's rendering and the register's definition: design :534 and :1333 render AC-111/AC-117 as bumping `schema_version`, while the register's GIVEN clauses (:1590, :1599), ADR-0072 :48 and the memo key (ADR-0043 :17, `activity id@version`) say `version`; `schema_version` elsewhere in both documents (design :650/:669, AC-135 :1890) is the per-artifact-type field under ADR-0006 — a different field on a different entity (rk-types, not rk-catalog). The register and ADR are the build sources and are consistent, so no wrong code results; the design sends the builder to files that do not exist and to the wrong join field for AC-111/AC-117's CI job.

`ac-packs-catalog.md` §1c carries a **second** doctor rule table — **AC-092–AC-099** — whose rows are configuration-time and zero-dispatch at the *pack* level

| AC-511 | 'a compiled-in payload wins over a payload-shaped cwd' (cut: contradicts §4.9) | the `--bare` half split from AC-488 | ports-dist |
It is still **cited rather than restated** — the area file owns the wording

concerns.why_before_step5: (i) Not Step 5. A Step 6 implementer must know reconcile.rs exists, where it lives after Step 2 and that 'validated' means 'ran over the corpus'; a verify-gate implementer reading AC-356 alone builds a class exemption the design refused; an rk-catalog CI check written from design 4.5 targets the wrong field; a builder reading the design is told AC-511 is contested when the binding register has settled it. (ii) AC-511 as defined is the criterion RUNBOOK 7c means, so the build is unaffected; the cost is operator time on five stale 're-read before changing' notes and an accepted-ADR/register contradiction on the convention every citation in the corpus relies on. (iii) A builder following the design's ownership rule is sent to files that do not exist, and the pre-build reconciliation at :362 has no place to happen; an implementer of AC-111/AC-117's changelog join working from the design would join on the wrong field.
concerns.remediation: (i) Amend the AC register's cut note and SM-051 to 'built and run in S0.2 (spikes/runner/src/reconcile.rs), not validated against engine decisions', the design rows to 'run over' rather than 'validated on', and add to RUNBOOK Step 6 the source location of reconcile.rs in redkiln-corpus at the pin (the same hazard phase1-deps OH-2 records for 7c's five files). Amend AC-356 in place (PROVISIONAL, not an ADR): strike the AND clause or relabel it 'design sketch under S-BIN block; not a criterion', and add ADR-0019 to its decisions line. Under the id-precedence rule the register governs: amend design 8.8 (line 1585) and 10.x (line 1969) to cite register 0.4 as the settlement, delete the 'unresolved' editorial note, and move AC-511 to ports-dist at design:362. Amend design lines 534 and 1333 to `version` and add one clause in section 5 distinguishing the activity `version` from the artifact-type `schema_version`. (ii) Amend the design (dated amendment) to withdraw the five 'unresolved' notes, citing AC §0.4 :122. Either partially supersede ADR-0085 with a record that licenses re-issue of a cut id under a §0.4-style hazard table, or record the six reuses as tracked convention debt in ADR-0085's consumer/backfill note. Do not renumber and do not edit ADR-0085. (iii) Amend the design in place (it is a design, not an ADR): replace each `ac-<area>.md §n` pointer with the register section (`acceptance-criteria.md §4.3` etc.), reword :349/:1968 to 'the register owns the wording', and re-home the :362 reconciliation to the register; add one sentence to AC §16 stating the area files were session scratch and were not committed. Correct design :534 and :1333 to `version` and add a note distinguishing the activity `version` (rk-catalog, ADR-0072) from the artifact-type `schema_version` (rk-types, AC-135).

concerns.title: Fully superseded ADR-0004 is the governing decision on 57 criteria in seven sections; ADR-0074 cited by none; §15.3 scopes the repair to §9
concerns.statement: [measured] 57 criteria across seven sections (§2: 3; §5: 6; §7: 7; §9: 27; §10: 9; §12: 3; §13: 2 — the §15.2 list; a body count reaches 58 with AC-317) carry ADR-0004 in their `decisions:` field. ADR-0004's frontmatter is `status: superseded`, `superseded_by: [0074]`, and the design (:908) says it is 'citable as history only'; no criterion cites ADR-0074, no criterion notes the supersession (AC-287's parenthetical concerns ADR-0015 → ADR-0020), and §15.2 hangs all 57 on ADR-0004 with no ADR-0074 row. The register's own repair note (§15.3 :6510) scopes the misdirection to 'the whole of §9' — 27 of the 57 — so 30 criteria in the type, kernel and adapter sections (seven of them harness ACs: AC-206, AC-208, AC-230, AC-231, AC-235, AC-236, AC-239) sit outside the repair it records. The same-day records ADR-0080, ADR-0082 and ADR-0088 carry `related: ["0004"]` while their bodies rely on ADR-0074's definitions (`Quarantined`, `Unverifiable`, the policy table) and cite 0074 only by legacy key ('D4's rev. 4 rebuild'); only ADR-0075 relates to 0074. The rule ('findings, not verdicts') survives into ADR-0074, so a builder following `superseded_by` lands on the right decision; the defect is a wrong pointer in 57 places of a register that is binding on the Phase-1 runbook.

concerns.statement: The register's criterion headers name `rk-kernel-verify`, `rk-select`, `rk-catalog`, `rk-packs`, `rk-port-toolchain`, `rk-store-artifacts`, `rk-policy` and `rk-doctor`: a strict header regex counts 28/22/18/12/4/2/2/2 = 90 criteria, and including PROVISIONAL/HUMAN GATE-prefixed headers reaches about 95 [measured]. None of the eight names occurs in RUNBOOK.md or the design (grep count 0 for each) [measured]; section 9.1 lists ten crate families and folds packs, policy and gates into `rk-kernel`; the register carries no note that its crate labels are area-file names [measured: no hit for 'crate label', 'module of', 'is not a crate']. Instruments such as 'a lattice CI monotonicity check' or an `rk-store` build test therefore point at a crate a builder cannot find, and no checkpoint can name `cargo test -p rk-select`.

concerns.title: No precedence rule ranks the design, AC register, SM register and RUNBOOK; the only ownership statement points at thirteen area files not in the tree
concerns.statement: Four documents each assert binding force -- the design is 'the authoritative architecture design' (over the proposal), the AC register is 'Binding on the Phase 1 build runbook' and 'decides nothing new', the SM register is 'Binding on Phase 1 telemetry', the ADR folder is 'the canonical location' -- and the RUNBOOK defers only to the design 'where the two disagree'. No document ranks the design's rendering of a criterion against the register's definition, or the AC register against the SM register: the design names neither register by path and neither register names the design (0 occurrences each) [measured]; ADR-0085 rules 1-9 fix formats and ids but rank no document against another. The design's only ownership statement assigns the criteria wording to 'the area files' (design:349, :1968), thirteen files that are not in the repository. The SM register's SM-015 note shows the gap biting: it declines to correct a target because doing so 'would make this document the authority on a figure AC-071 owns'. Where design and register renderings differ (the AC-511, AC-218/AC-428 and AC-173 cases elsewhere in this audit), a builder has no rule to pick, and the corpus has left three such differences standing rather than resolve them.

concerns.title: rk-git's and rk-store's Step-6 contracts are lists, not rules: unowned git ops (patch-id, merge, common-dir fallback), git-under-replay, target-repo hooks, trailer-affecting config and an undeclared trailer grammar, the answer record, `tree_hash` derivation, ADR-0018 vs AC-518 ownership, F20/2's extended-length path form, `busy_timeout` and transaction bounds, the event vocabulary, raw-payload retention and `Send`/`Sync` -- eighteen behaviours left to the implementer
concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) Eleven behaviours the Step 6 crates must exhibit are stated nowhere, each verified by grep over the design, register and ADR sets [measured]. rk-git: replay binds 'every port to its fake' (AC-006/AC-008) but git is a concrete crate, not a port, and nothing says whether tier-1 writes (trailers, empty commits, worktree add/remove, merge landing) execute, are suppressed or are journalled under replay; `git commit --trailer` runs the target repository's own hooks (a commit-msg hook rejecting a trailer-only message fails every transition and AC-162 then leaves no store row; a prepare-commit-msg hook can drop the trailer) while the corpus's 'no hooks' rule covers only redkiln-authored hooks (AC-182/AC-412); 'gate answered' is tier-1 git-first (design 681) yet `Gate:` is written only at open (684), AC-244..264 record the answer as an event, and no trailer key, ref or write mechanics exist for it; a killed run's still-present worktree has no reuse-or-recreate rule and a failed `worktree remove` no typed error or `doctor` row (`git worktree prune` appears only inside AC-190's fixture); F20/2's extended-length path defect — `canonicalize()` yields `\\?\D:\...`, git parses it as a URL, 'no code path reached the fetch successfully, ever' — binds no rk-git AC, its fix (`e3::git_remote_path`) is in a file 7c does not lift, and e3.jsonl already records `review_cwd` in the two forms a byte-equality reading of AC-195 would abort on; AC-245 demands `tree_hash` be 'that same tree object' with a dirty-worktree property test but no document says whether it is `write-tree` over a temporary index, whether untracked files enter it, or whether `HEAD^{tree}` is used when clean; and Checkpoint 6's hedge (1860) contradicts header row 23, 1343, 1830 and 2467, which make ADR-0091 unconditional. rk-store: ADR-0084 permits 'a single writer connection or a queued write path' with `busy_timeout` named fourteen times and never valued, no bound on the longest write transaction another process must wait out for AC-181's 'no lock error', and a queue that lets an F22-class kill drop an event AC-360 says no dispatch path may fail to append; the event log has no enumerated kind vocabulary, envelope or owning crate (18-20 backticked kinds across four documents; RUNBOOK 5.3's rk-types list omits an Event type); raw payloads are retained by construction (assistant text, `StepError::Schema.raw`, unrecognised events, argv carrying the 7,655-char card) with no sentence on what is verbatim, digested or never persisted; and port trait objects' `Send`/`Sync` bounds, which 7a must fix, are unstated. (ii) ADR-0077 assigns four read operations to gix and two write families to the exec wrapper, and its forbids block covers only worktree add/remove and trailer writes: AC-169's patch-id mechanism and the merge-queue merge (AC-196/197) have no owner, common-dir resolution sits on gix's read side while S-GIX/a tests exactly that interplay (so RUNBOOK:1813's 'a no-go costs nothing' is wrong for arm /a), and 'shallow clone by SHA for review checkouts' is a listed read while the same paragraph moves gix away from `gix-worktree-state` checkout [measured]. Both named trailer-write commands honour `trailer.ifexists`, `trailer.where`, `trailer.separators`, `commit.cleanup` and `core.commentChar`; nothing in ADR-0077, section 5.9, the ACs or RUNBOOK 6.2 pins them, and S-GIX/b's byte-identity oracle is the same config-honouring command over no named fixture [measured: the config keys occur only inside spikes/fixtures], so a repo with `trailer.ifexists=replace` silently collapses a second `Story:` trailer on tier-1 state. AC-165's 'declared trailer schema' is declared nowhere: the corpus holds 232 `Story:` values in three forms (201 project/slug, 22 bare RK-S ids, 9 free text), 15 prose-valued `Gate:` trailers and 49 `Fix:`/`Baseline-Repair:`/`Slice-Repair:` keys the design never names, and the only parser is spikes/runner/src/reconcile.rs, so AC-444's expected drift set is unpinned [measured over D:/repos/redkiln --all]. ADR-0018:38 and its forbids block key write refusal on the current worktree's HEAD; AC-518, the form that will be tested, keys it on the write's target and permits a run whose cwd is the user's checkout, so `redkiln answer` from a non-run worktree is refused by one implementer and landed as a trailer commit (AC-162/163) by the other, nothing narrows the ADR, and AC-181's two-process GIVEN does not say the runs are different items. AC-193 attributes stale-clone removal to `reconcile()`, which section 5.6 and AC-174 define as a git-to-store read; AC-427's THEN would be unambiguous if it named the pre-deletion store.

concerns.why_before_step5: (i) [inferred] None blocks Step 5 and any consistent choice satisfies the criteria as written; each is decided by whoever writes Step 6 first. Several shape public API a later record cannot cheaply reverse — whether rk-git needs a record/replay seam, the crate that owns the event enum (rk-types, Step 5, if anywhere), the `Send`/`Sync` bounds on `dyn` ports at 7a — and one (the path form) reproduces on the build platform a defect the corpus already paid for. Cheapest as one record before Step 6. (ii) Not Step 5. Step 6 builds rk-git to 'whatever S-GIX says' and Checkpoint 6 grep-asserts one shell-out file; without the operation set, the pinned config, the grammar and the ownership predicate, the single wrapper's scope, whether the review clone is bare, and the parser's AC-165/AC-444 fixtures are guesswork -- on the surface ADR-0077 itself calls 'a state-corruption class, not a bug class'. RUNBOOK 6.1 already plans the successor record where all of this belongs.
concerns.remediation: (i) One record before Step 6 — a successor or companion to ADR-0077/0018/0084 as each rule requires, never an edit — settling: git operations sit on the activity side of the split, each `reconcile()` result and write outcome journalled and served under replay through a `GitOps` seam (a struct, so AC-483 stands), with AC-006/AC-008 gaining 'and zero rk-git writes'; trailer commits run with `-c core.hooksPath=<empty dir>` (or `--no-verify` with the prepare-commit-msg residue documented) and AC-162's fault-injection fixture gains a rejecting commit-msg hook and a rewriting prepare-commit-msg hook; the answer's trailer key and value, the ref it lands on, and the plumbing (`commit-tree` + `update-ref`) used when no run-owned worktree exists, added to §5.4/§6.3.2 and AC §6.1; at entry a worktree registered to the item whose HEAD matches the run's branch is reused, otherwise removed and re-created, and a failed `worktree remove` is a typed error marking the item needs-operator and a `doctor` row listing orphans, with S-CANCEL-WIN's fixture as its test; every path handed to `git` or as a child `cwd` is the non-verbatim drive-letter form, verified by a Windows unit test, `git_remote_path` ported into the wrapper under Step 6.2 constraint 4 citing F20/2; the `tree_hash` algorithm (temporary index from worktree state including untracked-but-not-ignored files, `git write-tree`, same at open and answer) in design 6.3.2 and AC-245's Verified-by; ADR-0091 as 'S-GIX result and git-version floor, supersedes 0077 in part only on a go', deleting or qualifying the 1860 hedge. For rk-store, with R-SQLITE: the `busy_timeout` value and the rule that every write transaction is shorter than it (rebuild in a separate file then rename), one writer connection per process behind a mutex and no queue so append is synchronous with dispatch, a long-transaction fixture on AC-181; an event-kind table (kind, tier, payload fields, producing step) in design §5 or a new ADR and the owning crate named in RUNBOOK 5.3; per dispatch record which fields are verbatim and which digest-only, the child environment never persisted, a `doctor`/lint row asserting no credential-shaped field in the event schema — or an explicit 'redaction out of scope'; and port trait objects declared `Send` but not required `Sync`, with concurrent items stated once as separate processes. (ii) In the S-GIX successor record RUNBOOK 6.1 plans (a new ADR; ADR-0077 and ADR-0018 untouched): state the split as a rule -- git executes every mutation of `.git` and every operation gix does not expose at the pin -- with the current lists as examples; enumerate the wrapper's write set (worktree add/remove, `git add`/`commit --trailer`, empty commits, `interpret-trailers`, patch-id, merge/fast-forward on the integration ref, clone removal, `write-tree`); state whether the review clone is bare and by which implementation; make S-GIX/a's no-go fall back to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` through the wrapper; run every trailer write with trailer-affecting config pinned via `-c`, and run S-GIX/b's oracle under the same pinned config over a named fixture matrix (existing trailer block, no trailing newline, `---` divider, CRLF, duplicate token) with an AC asserting gix-parsed == git-written per fixture. Add a trailer grammar table to design section 5.4 or AC section 6.1 (key, value ABNF, column anchoring, verdict vocabulary, unknown-key rule, and 'a `Gate:` value that is not the (token, tree_hash, deadline) triple is legacy drift, counted but not a transition') and pin AC-444's expected drift counts from it. Add an AC under section 6.4 stating the target-based predicate once (a tier-1 write resolves the run-owned worktree from the store and commits there regardless of cwd; a write whose target is not run-owned is refused naming path and branch), record in the same successor ADR that ADR-0018's 'current worktree' wording is narrowed to it, and add 'of two different items' to AC-181's GIVEN. Reword AC-193 so removal is the entry step's clone-lifecycle action and `reconcile()` only reports the stale clone as drift; state in AC-172 whether `status` reconciles; name the pre-deletion store in AC-427's THEN with a Limit sentence 'not compared to the old redkiln's recorded outcomes -- F12: 1 of 101 recorded'.
concerns.owner: Step 6 implementer (rk-git, rk-store); Ryan (operator) for the retention and replay decisions; rk-kernel owner for the activity-side rule
