concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) RUNBOOK Step 6 gives no source location for reconcile.rs, the one sanctioned code import (design section 11:1653; ADR-0002), though Step 2 (canonical position 6, RUNBOOK:500) deletes spikes/runner before Step 6 (position 10) and the RUNBOOK contains 'reconcile.rs' zero times [measured]; after Step 2 the file survives only in redkiln-corpus at CORPUS_PIN. `git ls-tree -r 47faec9f` on the old redkiln lists 2,444 paths and zero `.rs` files, so AC-443's manifest of files 'imported from the old redkiln' describes a file that is this repo's spike artefact, not an import from that tree [measured]. AC-443's own instrument-limit note (AC:5521-5523) concedes the sanctioned import would not be detected by its hash tripwire, so the criterion's THEN is not broken; what is missing is the lift instruction and a truthful provenance origin. (ii) [measured] F12's Limits (:437) say 'the reconcile was not validated against the agent's decisions' (n = 1 recorded decision); the register cut AC-184's 'validated on 360 / 74' claim as unsupported by the brief (:2468), SM-081 (:916) records it as 'a slice-state result, not a validation of reconcile', and design §5.7 :725 disclaims it. Yet design :55/:184/:215/:252/:1653 still say 'validated', :1456 tags a not-yet-built replay's outcome ('reproducing 15 of 74 ... 74/74 slice states') [measured, F12], and the accepted ADR-0002 (:22, :57) and ADR-0003 (:64) assert it under a [measured] tag. Design :293, §0.1 row 37, ADR-0003 :22/:44/:64 and AC-483 :6006 further attribute 'measured behaviour' for trailers, worktrees, disposable clones and reconcile() to F12 and F19; both findings contain zero occurrences of 'worktree' or 'clone' — worktree behaviour is measured in F13/F16 (arm d, :586), and 'clone' occurs nowhere in spikes/FINDINGS.md, so disposable clones have no measuring finding at all. AC-444's replay test compares the product's reconcile against s02-reconcile.jsonl, which is the spike's own reconcile.rs output: a self-consistency regression, not a validation, and the AC's 'without manual annotation' wording hides that. The AC-184 cut over-corrects the other way — a Rust reconcile was built (spikes/runner/src/reconcile.rs produced F12); what was never done is validation. The decision (import reconcile.rs) stands either way.

concerns.title: ADR-0077's gitoxide citations point at sources that say the opposite: 'shallow clone by SHA, confirmed in gitoxide #2309' cites a thread showing a panic (the API is `PrepareFetch::with_revision`, PR #2824) and crate-status.md lists 'parse trailers' as an unchecked box (docs.rs gix-object 0.64.1 `BodyRef::trailers()` exists); S-GIX has no clone arm and its /b read half is discharged, leaving the executed test
concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) ADR-0077 :48 and architecture-design :743/:2014, RUNBOOK :1820 and evidence-augmentation :161 rest the hybrid's read-side bet - 'shallow clone by SHA for review checkouts' - on gitoxide discussion #2309. That thread (2025-12-28) reports 'I get a panic from inside gix ... we map by name only and have no object-id in refspec', the maintainer's reply that `with_ref_name()` 'really only wants a reference right now', and its fix PR #2310 closed unmerged [documented, first verification of a self-flagged row]. The capability does exist at the pin, through a different API: docs.rs gix 0.87.1 `PrepareFetch::with_revision` ('Fetch only revision and check it out with a detached HEAD ... or a full object ID'), landed by PR #2824 on 2026-08-05 and combinable with `with_shallow` - weeks old at the pin. Trailer parsing is CONFIRMED at source (gix-object 0.64.1 `BodyRef::trailers()`), so only the clone citation drifts. RUNBOOK §6.1 registers S-GIX/a (common dir) and S-GIX/b (trailer writing) and nothing exercises the clone path AC-339's disposable checkout depends on. (ii) ADR-0077, the design's git-layer table and evidence-augmentation row 8 all cite gitoxide's crate-status.md as the source that 'documents trailer parsing'. crate-status.md line 259 lists 'parse trailers' as an UNCHECKED box under gix-object commit decode; it does not document the capability. The capability nonetheless exists: docs.rs for gix-object 0.64.1 (the sub-crate behind the pinned gix 0.87.1) exposes BodyRef::trailers(), without_trailer() and message_blocks(), so the read-side bet is right and its citation is wrong. The same docs.rs read finds no trailer-writing method on MessageRef or BodyRef, and gix-actor's write helpers are for signatures, not trailers, so the absence the corpus flagged UNVERIFIED ('the highest-value single check in the list') is now verified against a fetched listing; the executed-test arm of S-GIX/b remains owed. concerns.title: An equivalent mutant survives re-execution, so ADR-0074's `mutation-survived` class can block on a no-op mutation the machine cannot filter
concerns.statement: ADR-0074 computes the evidence class in Rust: '`mutation-survived` iff a mutation was applied and the named suite stayed green', and the policy table makes `reproduced` and `mutation-survived` block. Standard mutation-testing semantics, which PRIOR-ART s5 already adopts for the measurement side ('exclude equivalent mutants from the denominator; prefer revert-the-fix-keep-the-test'), include the equivalent mutant: a mutation that does not change behaviour survives every suite. Re-execution therefore confirms the finding's premise (the mutant survived) without confirming its claim (the suite has a gap), and the machine-confirms rule that ADR-0074 relies on to strip the reviewer's false blocks does not filter this case. cargo-mutants (27.1.0, June 2026) is live, and equivalent-mutant detection remains an open research line (arXiv 2607.00511). Neither the ADR's clause 2 nor its policy table names equivalence triage or restricts the class to reverted-fix mutants. [inferred from documented semantics]

anchors.quote: `mutation-survived` iff a mutation was applied and the named suite stayed green
`reproduced` and `mutation-survived` block; `narrowed-pin` blocks only under a strict weight; `advisory` and `Unverifiable` never block.
| 3 | S0.1 adopts mutation-testing methodology: exclude equivalent mutants from the denominator; prefer revert-the-fix-keep-the-test as the mutation source; use existing tooling | §5 |

concerns.title: AC-388's per-sibling stagger chain is not the vendor's mechanism (hold until first response begins, cap 5 s, release together); SM-114 tests it wrong
concerns.statement: AC-388 requires that in a fan-out 'the first is dispatched alone and each remaining sibling's dispatch timestamp is at least `i` after the previous one', citing 'platform docs' for 'stagger identical-prefix siblings ~5 s so the first pays the write'. platform.claude.com says only 'wait for the first response before sending subsequent requests', with no number; the 5 s is Claude Code's workflow-runtime default: 'holds all but the first until the first agent's response begins, then releases the held agents together ... caps the hold at CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS milliseconds, 5000 by default' [documented; Wayback 2026-09-02 identical]. That is a capped wait-for-first-token with simultaneous release, not a serial (n-1) x i chain. SM-114's decision rule (i = 5 s vs i = 0, n >= 50 sibling pairs, 'AC-388's stagger requirement is dropped if no difference') therefore never tests the vendor's scheduler, and a null result would drop a rule the vendor's mechanism might have supported. Since rk-kernel spawns `claude -p` itself, the CLI's workflow stagger does not apply to redkiln's fan-out at all; the kernel must implement whichever shape it chooses.

anchors.quote: **AC-388** — `rk-kernel` scheduler · evidence: §4.3 fan-out row [documented: stagger identical-prefix siblings ~5 s so the first pays the write; platform docs]; F13 [measured: 69% of the prefix is shared across directories]

concerns.title: Claude Code `defer` (`tool_deferred`) shipped in 2.1.89 on 2026-03-31 and is documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks; evidence-augmentation's 'allow/deny only, unverified' and the competitor row assert the opposite, the section 6.6 survey omits the harness's own durable per-tool-call pause, and no record priced tool-grain suspend-and-resume against ADR-0087
concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) evidence-augmentation Claim 2 asserts that Claude Code hook permission decisions are 'allow/deny only' and that the April-2026 `tool_deferred` mechanism 'could not be corroborated in first-party docs'. The first-party hooks page documents four PreToolUse outcomes (allow, deny, ask, defer) with precedence deny > defer > ask > allow, a 'Defer a tool call for later' section, `stop_reason: "tool_deferred"`, no timeout, and the session persisted on disk until `claude -p --resume <session-id>`; the CHANGELOG files it under 2.1.89, npm-published 2026-03-31 [documented]. The corpus self-flagged this UNVERIFIED and its first verification fails on both halves. No AC or ADR anchors Claim 2, and architecture-design :854 has already narrowed the novelty claim to the tree-hash binding, so no decision falls. Two things do: the §6.6 durable-systems survey (:841-:848) omits the one durable, resumable, per-tool-call pause in the harness the product drives, and it carries no built-in deadline, which is the Restate shape; and ADR-0087's rejected 'hold the process open' option has a vendor-provided third shape - exit with the pending call preserved, resume by session id across a fresh process - which the design never priced against F38's 0.45-0.78x resume cost. AC-186/AC-400 forbid `--resume` on redkiln's own CLI, not on the child. (ii) The corpus self-flagged the `tool_deferred` / `defer` question as unverified and left the competitor row on the negative reading. The first verification fails it: the live first-party hooks reference documents `permissionDecision (allow/deny/ask/defer)` with '"defer" exits gracefully so the tool can be resumed later', and the official CHANGELOG records it shipping in 2.1.89 ('headless sessions can pause at a tool call and resume with -p --resume to have the hook re-evaluate') [documented]. A Wayback capture of 2026-09-07 already carries it, so evidence-augmentation:283's 'the current first-party hooks doc shows no trace' was false on the corpus's own date, and :124's two predicates ('hook permission decisions are allow/deny only'; '`/resume` resumes a whole session, not a paused tool call') are false today [documented]. The design's differentiation claim survives because it was already narrowed to the tree-hash binding inside an AI-coding-specific backlog tool (architecture-design:854) and ADR-0087's suspension is at step grain across a kernel-owned process boundary; but the Claude adapter now has a harness-native, headless, tool-grain suspend-and-resume primitive that no record evaluated, and the design's `PreToolUse` rule (architecture-design:1580) was written on the assumption that a hook can only allow or deny.

anchors.quote: Claude Code hook permission decisions are allow/deny only (`PermissionDenied` can set `retry:true` for the *model* to retry, not for a human to intervene) ... **Several 2026 blogs claiming an April-2026 `tool_deferred` mechanism could not be corroborated in first-party docs** — treat as unverified

Did Claude Code's April-2026 `tool_deferred` / defer permission decision ever ship? | Several SEO blogs describe it; the current first-party hooks doc shows no trace. Changelogs were not checked. | **Yes** — Anthropic's changelog/release notes.

This design's novelty claim is **not** "nobody ships stage-gated, mid-run, resumable human approval on a durable work item" ... The claim that survives is the narrower one: **in an AI-coding-specific backlog or spec tool**, and on the *binding* rather than the gate
### Option — hold the process open across the gate ... Rejected on prior evidence, not on P8 ... Nothing may depend on a process surviving; every wait is a durable mark plus a later read.
The `PreToolUse` deny survives as a **stateless predicate** — it reads only its own tool input and references no stage, run, session or item state | DECIDED by proposal §4.9 | AC-505

2. Resume must cross a real process boundary. A reload that reads state back in-process is not a valid implementation of this decision and is not evidence for it, because the risk being managed is that a *fresh* process reconstructs something different.

(ii) Step 5 builds the kernel, not the Claude adapter, so nothing is built wrong; but the adapter's dispatch contract and ADR-0087's successor will be written against a competitor table that is factually wrong about the harness the product dispatches to, and an option (harness-level defer at a tool call, resumed with `-p --resume`) would be silently absent from the option set.

(2) architecture-design §6.6 table (:841-:848) gains a row 'Claude Code hook defer' - no token object (session id + pending tool call in the transcript), no built-in deadline, resumed by `claude -p --resume`; the sentence 'every platform this pass could actually read mints a single-use signal and guarantees a terminal event' is narrowed accordingly. (3) Discharge the placement question as a named spike, not prose: S-DEFER (consumer: ADR-0087 gate placement and rk-adapter-claude's AC-215 stall guard) - drive a PreToolUse hook returning defer under the pinned CLI, kill the parent, resume in a fresh process, and record survival, drift and resume cost against F38; a go narrows ADR-0087 by successor record only. (4) No supersession of ADR-0017/0087 until S-DEFER reports. (ii) Append a dated erratum to evidence-augmentation §1 row 'Claim 2' and §5 row 283 (the pass is a dated record; do not rewrite the rows) stating: defer shipped in 2.1.89, is documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later, and was present on 2026-09-07. Register a reading-plus-fixture spike (name it R-DEFER; consumer: the Claude adapter's dispatch contract under ADR-0010's successor and ADR-0087's successor) that answers two questions on the pinned `claude` version: whether a `defer` from a settings-based `PreToolUse` hook fires under `-p` (F2 measured 2 hook events per dispatch, so the fixture exists), and whether a deferred tool call resumed with `-p --resume` preserves the tree-hash binding the design requires. Until it runs, the differentiation sentence at architecture-design:854 stands unchanged and ADR-0087 stands unchanged; the erratum names R-DEFER as the discharge, per ADR-0012.

concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) Summary rows and acceptance-set ranges overstate what their detailed sections say. [measured] (1) RUNBOOK:1902 gives Step 7a's acceptance set as AC-480-AC-519 minus AC-239/AC-496/AC-502 only; the range still contains AC-501/AC-503-AC-506 (rk-plugin-gen, Phase 2 per AC:6372), AC-507/AC-508/AC-510 (GitHub and mdBook adapters, Phase 3), retired AC-513 (AC:112) and the six CONDITIONAL criteria AC-512/AC-514-AC-517/AC-519 that design:1630 says 'are not runbook requirements' -- up to 16 criteria with no Phase-1 instrument. (2) RUNBOOK:2007's Step 5 set spans 'AC-080-AC-119' though AC-119 was never allocated (AC:112, :1295 -- the only one of the RUNBOOK's 77 cited AC ids with no definition), and the same sentence's 'AC-040-AC-079' subtracts the P1-blocked rows but not retired AC-075. (3) Design section 0.1 row 32 says 'AC-480..AC-519 are borrowed-failure criteria and every measure in the area starts with no baseline'; section 8.8:1563 narrows the first to the distribution half (AC-480/481/483/484 are Phase-1 CI assertions, RUNBOOK:1775) and SM-154 carries a measured $56.47 baseline (SM:1044 correctly says seven of eight). (4) AC section 0.3:75 says 'AC-236's gate half is distinct and is not duplicated' while AC-038:550-552 asserts the same gate-half behaviour, section 0.3 has no AC-038/AC-236 row, and design:342 lists AC-036/037/038/236 together; the clause is at best ambiguous ('not duplicated by AC-037') and the twin is missing either way. (5) Design section 5.11:778 claims 'Every row resolves to a spike with a named consumer in section 10'; of its ten rows only three name a spike (S-BIN, S-GIX, P8's arms), and section 10:1898 itself says the rest resolve to a recorded decision. (ii) [measured] Nine small pointer defects, all one-line fixes. F40-DRAFT.md landed 2026-09-10 (009a4ec) and is cited at 22/23/26 anchors in the design/SM/RUNBOOK, but the design's Inputs line (:3) and sources row (:1986) still enumerate the drafts as F29–F38 (+F39), one row below a brief row that says F1–F40; SM :5 attributes 'F1–F38' to spikes/FINDINGS.md, which holds F1–F28; design :1985 says '§C.1–C.13 ... C.13 is F39's, appended' in the same row whose ledger clause records 'F40 added 2026-09-10' (the brief has 14 items, design :218 maps C.1–C.14); design :904 says 'nine blocked rows of §0.1' where :15 counts ten (the `stale_policy` row was added in a627547). RUNBOOK 7b's acceptance set 'AC-080–AC-119' includes AC-119, which the register marks unallocated, and the same range pattern in 7a/7b/7c sweeps in all six ids ids.json lists as dangling (AC-075, AC-119, AC-207, AC-255, AC-297, AC-513), so a coverage script keyed on the ranges reports six phantoms. AC-095 :1438 cross-references AC-014 (the memo-key miss property test) for the dispatch-time StructuredOutput refusal and flags the reference as unverified — the intended criterion is AC-205 (§0.3 :91); SM-006's only firing condition (:81) files an overage admission against AC-027 (zero re-dispatch after a StepError) when the pre-spawn refusal is AC-221 (:2863), so a defect routed to AC-027 would be closed as not-a-retry. METHOD-S §7 (2026-09-09, :951-960) registers four of five S-BIN items as carrying a source/test `text_diff` and states the register rows 'are qualified accordingly', and :1017-1023 names two candidate captures producers with the manual /ue-verify route (17 PNGs at the pin) the one in use; design :22 still names only the never-run automation comparison, and :607/:1862 still read 'no diff' unqualified — no file in references/ or RUNBOOK contains 'not diff-free' or 'four of five'. (iii) Each item is one document carrying a figure or status in two states because a correction landed in one place and the restatement was read off the sentence rather than re-derived, the drift class design 0.1's header (:15) already had to correct once [measured unless tagged]. SM register :749, :988 and :1257 say the '>=12 of 23 (52%)' figure was cut as fabricated (with an arithmetically wrong rationale: 5/23 is F24's 21.7%, a different count), while :1437 and AC 15 (:6558) restore it as real, sourced to proposal 1 and design-recommendation :38, so whether SM-100 has a baseline (at most 11/23 pinned) depends on which row is read; AC:1285 says SM-021 'still has no target and no baseline' eleven lines after AC:1274 and the SM register's same-day amendment (:176, :1112, :1125, :1313, :1381, :1414) give it a partial specificity baseline and recount 59 to 58; SM:133 sets SM-015's target at >=5 draws where AC-071's precondition (:165, :1112) and the design's corrected sites read >=10, SM:136 deferring to 'the area owner' - ac-selection.md - which does not exist [documented]. Design:904 counts 'nine blocked rows of 0.1' after :15 raised the table to ten on 2026-09-10; design:1985 says the brief's C runs to C.13 and :3's Inputs omit F40-DRAFT, which the body cites 22 times, against :218 and brief:143 (C.14 is F40's); RUNBOOK:913-914 says 'F29-F39 live as drafts' on a 2026-09-09 `ls F3*` glob that cannot match F40, which :9 and 26 other lines cite; the SM id range is 'SM-001..SM-154 plus SM-157' (AC:3), 'SM-001-SM-156 plus SM-157' (design:3, :1990), and SM-155/156 are 'reserved to ports-dist' (AC:598) or 'belong to no area at all' (SM:31, AC:5975); AC:120 still cuts AC-323's original on 'its evidence, GATE-05, does not exist' after 15 (:6551) restored GATE-05 as real (scorecard:141), the second cut ground standing but the original never re-asked; design:135 records the AFK output committed at e3b0bac then closes 'Residual: nothing from the AFK session was committed', citing brief E, which post-correction says the opposite; RUNBOOK:446-447, :548 and :2464 say 'three filled panels' while :723, :805-807 and :2458 retain arm D unfilled at `labeller: FILL-ME` by amendment 9. None has a build consequence; each is what a builder reads first.

concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) 7a names AC-480–AC-519 with only AC-239/496/502 excluded (1902-1903). The register's own area note (6372) phases AC-501..506 to Phase 2 and AC-507/508/510 to Phase 3; AC-512, 514-517 carry CONDITIONAL and AC-519 'partly CONDITIONAL' in their headers, and design 1587/1630 says those rows 'bind on nothing and are not runbook requirements'; AC-513 is retired [measured]. AC-497 — in range, PROVISIONAL, 'may be implemented' — asserts the Toolchain port returns a typed `ChangeSummary` value while Step 5.3's checkpoint (1763) greps rk-types for the identifier and demands zero, and no document says where a shape-only type may live; 5.3 names AC-154 as not evaluable and never AC-497. 7c states 'AC-320–AC-359' flat (2071) without the 'minus the P1-blocked rows' form 7b uses (2006), although AC-356's Verified-by is a `ChangeSummary` schema test §6.5.4 forbids until S-BIN reports. 7c's AC-280–AC-319 includes AC-312 (a release regression corpus with negative-control and seeded fixtures) while ADR-0074:89 forbids 'shipping the fixture family without the presented-as-already-approved arm'; that arm (S-SUBTLE-CB) is registered, unrun and unsized, and no RUNBOOK step names AC-312, the corpus regression job or the arm's framing fixtures [measured]. Whether 'with the arm' means its paired presentations are authored (ADR-0088 clause 1) or S-SUBTLE-CB has run is unstated. (ii) Step 7a's acceptance set (RUNBOOK:1902) names AC-480 to AC-519 whole, unlike its five sibling steps (RUNBOOK:1774, 1863, 2006, 2118), which carve out non-evaluable rows; the RUNBOOK never mentions CONDITIONAL, `rk-plugin-gen` or distribution [measured]. It therefore binds a Phase-1 sign-off to AC-501/503-506 (`rk-plugin-gen`, Phase 2, 'nothing in this sub-section is checkable before then'), AC-507/508/510 (Phase 3), the CONDITIONAL AC-512/514-517 and part of AC-519 that the register calls UNBUILDABLE, and retired AC-513: fourteen of thirty-seven named ids [measured]. The design says reading the CONDITIONAL rows as runbook requirements is 'the exact failure this subsection exists to prevent'; the RUNBOOK does exactly that. The finder's two further claims fall: the AC-502 exclusion on S-CODEX grounds is correct (AC:185), and line 1877's 'one real adapter' restates the port rule as design:1852 does, imprecise in a Phase-1 step but not a contradiction of design:246. Checkpoint 7a's commands are unaffected: wrong record, not wrong build.

Add one sentence to AC-312 and to 7c's acceptance paragraph stating which reading holds: (a) AC-312 is PROVISIONAL on S-SUBTLE-CB and ships in Phase 1 with the arm's framing-variant fixtures authored but unrun — then add the authoring task to a step and price it in §10.5; or (b) ADR-0074's forbids applies at the first release shipping the family and AC-312 is deferred to it — then re-label AC-312 in §9's state line ('36 binding · 1 provisional'). concerns.title: Statistics tagged [measured] or settled do not reproduce under the registered two-sided Wilson interval: MCC +0.978 is +0.957 (ten sites); '~60 positives' is 73; F27's '~30%' is 56-66%; F37's 3/3 vs 0/3 overlap, so section 4.4(1) had zero power at n=3 and S-P7B's n=10 is powerless too; McNemar p=0.625 is bound to the detection tie at nine sites; F19's 3.6x is mis-inferred from CI overlap; SM-086's 'n >= 500' is 637
concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) Five statistical figures tagged [measured] do not reproduce under the corpus's own conventions (Wilson 95%, z=1.96, METHOD-P:17). (a) MCC +0.978 for E3 arm (a) at FP 1/23: the matrix tp=23 fn=0 fp=1 tn=22 gives +0.957; the same formula reproduces the corpus's +0.839 (fp=4) and +0.917 (fp=2), an exhaustive search finds no 23-item matrix at 0.978, and the figure stands in ten places (annotation sheet :131; design :31, :123, :179, :956, :1049, :1819, :1873; RUNBOOK :881; rfc-amendment :223) with no matrix beside it. (b) 'Roughly 60 positives are needed for a lower bound above 0.95' (F39:92; RUNBOOK :123/:969/:2396 tagged [measured]; ~15 restatements): the first n with Wilson(k=n) lower > 0.95 is 73 (n=60 gives 0.940; 92 with continuity correction; Clopper-Pearson 72). (c) F27's 'stable at n=2-3 tolerates a true flip rate up to ~30%' (FINDINGS:1686; design :79, brief :42, SM :18, ADR-0074 :96, ADR-0088 :91): Wilson 95% upper on 0/3 is 0.56 and on 0/2 is 0.66; a 30% rate leaves a 34% chance of no flip in 3 draws, so ~30% corresponds to no conventional level and its derivation is undisclosed. (d) F37:39 says 3/3 [0.44, 1.00] against 0/3 [0.00, 0.56] is the only non-overlapping pair -- they share [0.44, 0.56], so section 4.4(1) is strictly unfalsifiable at n=3, the stronger claim F37:1 and design :24/:103 already make; section 2 and Limits 1 contradict them. (e) F19's 3.6x (9/79 vs 3/95): the ratio is right (3.61) but 'overlapping intervals, not separated' is the CI-overlap fallacy -- log-RR 95% CI [1.01, 12.9], Fisher p=0.039 -- a conservative-direction mis-inference used as SM section 0 rule 3's paradigm of small-n discipline; SM :923/:925/:1182 also print the upper bound as 20.2% where 9/79 gives 20.3%. (a), (c), (e) are NEW; (b), (d) sharpen recorded limits that carry the wrong number as fact. (ii) [measured] Recomputed with the programme's registered interval — two-sided Wilson at z = 1.96, the `wilson()` in spikes/p1/score-arm-d-panel.py that reproduces F39's 0.65 for 7/7 and 0.26 for 0/11 — three sizing statements the corpus treats as settled are wrong. (i) 'Roughly 60 positives are needed for a lower bound above 0.95' (F39 Limits 1; restated in the design, both registers, RUNBOOK :123/:969 tagged [measured], the brief, ADR-0089, the change-classification and two handoffs): for k = n the lower bound is n/(n + 3.8416), so 60/60 gives 0.940 and the scorer's own verdict line (:120) would print STAYS; the bound first clears 0.95 at 73 all-correct positives (72 under Clopper-Pearson); 'roughly 60' holds only for a one-sided z = 1.645 that nothing registers. (ii) F37 :39 and ADR-0080 :52 say the only n = 3 pair that fails to overlap is 3/3 against 0/3, 'the maximum possible separation'; 3/3 = [0.439, 1.000] and 0/3 = [0.000, 0.561] overlap on [0.439, 0.561], so no n = 3 pair can separate under METHOD-P §4.4(1) — the criterion had zero power, not 'almost none' (the §0.1/RUNBOOK phrase 'overlaps by construction' is the correct one; HANDOFF:223 repeats the error). ADR-0080 :104's claim that at n = 10 per cell a 1-in-10 effect is resolvable is false under the same criterion: 0/10 = [0, 0.278] overlaps 1/10 = [0.018, 0.404] and 3/10 = [0.108, 0.603]; 6/10 is the first cell to separate, so the registered S-P7B design (design :1870, 'n = 10 per cell') is powerless for the effect it names and would spend a multiple of $131.62 to reproduce an unfalsifiable comparison. (iii) SM-086's target reads 'once n allows an interval that excludes it (n ≥500 blocks)': 0/500 has upper 0.762%, which does not exclude 0.6%; the smallest n at which 0/n excludes it is 637 (0/636 → 0.6004%), and any observed false block pushes it higher (1/700 → 0.805%); the register's rule 3 (every quoted interval computed here) was not applied to the n. No Phase-1 code restates any of the three, but S-FACET's corpus, S-P7B's re-run and SM-086's calibration claim would each be sized from a number that is powerless at its own n — the defect class RB-GC-010 already counts four instances of. (iii) [measured] F23 (:1172-1179) states that detection was 'identical and at ceiling ... zero discordant pairs' and that McNemar's test was run on the CLEAN verdict discordant pairs, 3 vs 1 — exact two-sided p = 2·5/16 = 0.625, reproduced from e3.jsonl; on detection 23/23 vs 23/23 the test has no value. The measurement doctrine that opens the SM register (§0 :12), design :33/:71/:960/:1554, AC :3937/:6408, ADR-0001 :56, ADR-0080 :192, ADR-0088 :42 and the brief :74 all write 'detection 23/23 vs 23/23 at McNemar p=0.625', and AC-283's repair note (:3599) asserts that 'that figure is a detection comparison between E3 arms'; only HANDOFF:152 binds it to the co-primary FPR. Separately, the DECIDED §0.1 row 'False-positive rates and MCCs from E3' settles arm (a) at FP 1/23 / MCC +0.978; on the corpus's own construction (46-item matrix, spikes/results/audit-e3.py :122, which reproduces F21's +0.917 and F23's +0.839) tp=23 fn=0 fp=1 tn=22 gives +0.957, and +0.978 reproduces only as sqrt(0.957) or from a doubled matrix; no corpus document contains 0.957. The +0.978 is restated at design :31/:123/:179/:956/:1049/:1819/:1873, RUNBOOK :881 and rfc-amendment :223 — census agreement on the wrong number. Neither error changes the gate's design (design :1049), but the register's construction rule is introduced with a statistic attached to the wrong comparison, one repair note codifies it, and a DECIDED row cites a miscomputed calibration figure.

SM-086: amend the target to 'n ≥ 640 adjudicated blocks at zero false blocks (Wilson upper < 0.6%, computed here); more if any false block is observed', or state it as a bound rather than an exclusion. (iii) Amend SM §0 :12 and every restatement to 'detection 23/23 vs 23/23 (no discordant pairs, no test); CLEAN FP 4/23 vs 2/23, McNemar exact p = 0.625 on the 3-vs-1 discordant pairs'; correct AC-283's repair note. concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) ADR-0086 :90 claims a same-day crates.io read on 2026-09-08 that 'strictly dominates' the charter. On that date `temporalio-sdk` was 1.0.0 (published 2026-09-04, release note 'the Rust SDK is now considered stable'; every 0.x tag marked pre-release) on `temporalio-sdk-core` 0.9.0, not 'v0.5.0, Public Preview, updated June 2026'; and `graph-flow` was 0.8.0 (2026-09-07), not 0.6 [documented]. The mandatory-dependency list ADR-0086 :20/:91 attributes to v0.6 is exactly 0.8.0's: at 0.6.0 sqlx ^0.8.6 was REQUIRED, so the charter's 'hard-depends on sqlx+postgres' was true when written and became false only on 2026-09-07; and at 0.8.0 `postgres` is a DEFAULT feature, so 'no required database' holds only with default-features = false. :55 orders every document to 'correct to the facts above, naming the live crates and versions', which propagates the wrong versions. Riders: the charter's 'dbos crate is 12 lines with 39 downloads' is stale (dbos 0.5.0, 2026-09-09, sqlx+postgres required); 'iopsystems/durable ... no version or release tags visible' is false on the tags endpoint (v0.6.2, durable-v0.6.0) - it has tags but no GitHub Releases. The exclusion (server mandate; in-memory not durable; Postgres + WASM) does not turn on any of these and is, if anything, strengthened by postgres-by-default. (ii) ADR-0086 re-argues the durable-execution exclusion 'on facts that hold' and dates every fact to a live read on 2026-09-08, yet the facts it names were already stale that day: temporalio-sdk was at 1.0.0 on temporalio-sdk-core 0.9.0 (published 2026-09-04, release notes declare the SDK stable), not 'v0.5.0, June 2026, Public Preview'; graph-flow was at 0.7.0 (0.8.0 on 2026-09-07), not v0.6, and its postgres feature is enabled by default, the exact shape the ADR's feature-flag clause guards against; iopsystems/durable has no Releases but does carry version tags (v0.6.2, durable-v0.6.0). The decision driver 'Rust remains second-class across every first-party durable-execution SDK checked' is false today: Temporal's Rust SDK is GA and DBOS Inc. published a first-party `dbos` crate (0.5.0, 2026-09-09) that is a library with no server, so 'the server is the arbiter' does not cover it either. The registered open item (a time-skipping local test server) is now answered: `WorkflowEnvironment::start_local` exists in the SDK's testing feature. None of this reopens the exclusion, which survives on ADR-0003 (dbos hard-requires sqlx/postgres; Temporal still needs a server) and on the ADR's own ban on re-litigating maturity, but a record whose stated purpose is citability now carries four stale currency facts, one false driver and one missing option row. [documented]

concerns.title: 'No first-party source' for the thiserror/anyhow split is false in six live places: the crate author's own anyhow README and thiserror docs document it, and Microsoft M-APP-ERROR exists with a named divergence on in-repo crates; the stricter 'never in a library's public API' stays a house rule
concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) ADR-0083:72 and :121, architecture-design:1673, :1721 and :2051, and evidence-augmentation:55 all state that the thiserror-in-libraries / anyhow-in-application split rests on 'two 2026 practitioner blogs and no first-party source'. The canonical statement of the split is the crate author's own: dtolnay's anyhow README, 'Comparison to thiserror' ('Use Anyhow if you don't care what error type your functions return ... This is common in application code. Use thiserror if you are a library'), and thiserror's docs.rs page ('See also the anyhow library for a convenient single error type to use in application code') [documented]. The evidence is first-party and strengthens the ADR. What remains house convention is the stricter clause: the README recommends 'application code', it does not forbid `anyhow::Error` in a library's public API, so ADR-0083:72's 'never' stays a rule the project sets, not one the source documents. anyhow 1.0.104 (architecture-design:1673) is current on crates.io. (ii) ADR-0083 and the design's dependency table adopt 'thiserror in library crates, anyhow confined to binary crates' as a house convention 'corroborated by two 2026 practitioner blogs and by no first-party source'. A vendor guideline now exists (Microsoft, generated 2026-08-19) and largely agrees, with two named divergences: M-APP-ERROR lets 'crates in your own repository exclusively used from your application' use anyhow/eyre, where the ADR forbids anyhow in every non-binary crate; and M-ERRORS-CANONICAL-STRUCTS recommends situation-specific error structs with Backtrace rather than enums for library errors. The ADR's stricter rule is defensible for adapter crates a second binary may share (it already notes the cost at :99), but the evidence tag 'thin, no first-party source' is now wrong and should read 'vendor-corroborated with a named divergence'. [documented]

concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) ADR-0087 clause 3 and its forbids line ('measured, it costs less'), SM-052/SM-073's baselines and AC-266's provisional note rest on F38's 0.45x/0.55x/0.78x. [measured] The numerator is P8's `resume_tokens` = summed `output_tokens` of the resumed dispatch (main.rs:3288; 8,408/10,314/14,579) and the denominator is F28's 18,603 `cache_creation_input_tokens` on a post-TTL re-read whose own output was 348-933 tokens (main.rs:3349 divides by a hard-coded 18600.0; FINDINGS:1714's column header is 'cache creation on resume'). On the field SM-052/SM-073/AC-266 name as their instrument the same P8 dispatches recorded cache_creation of 84,960/49,468/46,961 = 4.57x/2.66x/2.52x of 18,603 -- above the pre-registered >1.5x kill, with the cross-fixture caveat that P8's prompt is larger than F28's ~36k review prefix. Design:735 mislabels the three figures as `cache_creation` tokens, ADR-0087:17 mislabels F28's as 'output tokens', and the ratio is restated roughly 27-35 times across seven to nine files (the '88 restatements' one finder claimed did not reproduce). A second over-read of F28 stands at design:828, AC:3136 and SM:588 -- 'F28 proves a keep-warm dispatch buys nothing' -- though F28 ran no keep-alive arm and its own correction (FINDINGS:1800-1805) credits the programme's constant unrelated dispatching for the 48% that stayed warm; what F28 bounds is the rewrite (~18.6k-29.7k per gate). METHOD-P section 5.4 pre-registered 'resume cost in tokens' without fixing the token type, so P8-B inherits the driver metric. (ii) [measured] F38's 8,408 / 10,314 / 14,579 are `usage.output_tokens` of the first post-resume dispatch (the runner sums `output_tokens`; p8.jsonl rows for issue-81/74/79 copy them into `resume_tokens`), as F38's own table header says; F28's 18,603 is `cache_creation_input_tokens` ('cache creation on resume', FINDINGS.md :1714-1718; every 18603 in spikes/results is a cache_creation field). The ratio quoted in §0.1 row 29, §3.5, AC-013, AC-039, SM-002 :49 and ADR-0087 therefore divides unlike counters, and ADR-0087 :88 mischaracterises F28's figure as 'output tokens'. SM-002 :48 names `cache_creation_input_tokens` as its instrument; on that instrument the same three dispatches read 49,468 (issue-81) / 84,960 (issue-74) / 46,961 (issue-79) — 2.5×–4.6× of 18,603, summed over agentic turns so not a clean comparator either — the side of METHOD-P §5.4's >1.5× line the pre-registration anticipated. SM-002 as written cannot be evaluated against its own baseline, and ADR-0087's provisional mid-graph placement rests on a 'does not fire' verdict for a criterion whose units were never fixed. (iii) Design 6.3.6:900, 0.1 row 29 and 7.10 rule that 'mid-graph gates are cheaper than stage gates' may not be written without n=3 and the missing baseline in the same sentence, and design:894 takes the decision 'because it is safe under either answer'; the accepted ADR governing the row states the forbidden sentence in its title (restated wherever the ADR is listed by title), in Decision clause 3 ('Measured, it is cheaper') and in its forbids block with no qualifier, and its 'what would change this decision' names a >1.5x cost result - so the decision is not safe under either answer per the ADR - while ADR-0087:17 attaches activity-terminal escalation to that kill where METHOD-P 5.4:229-230 attaches it to the lost-output kill and only a pricing change to the cost kill [documented]. Separately, design 1.2:127 calls F37's 3.66x and the decisions log's 4.4x 'two numbers, one quantity', refuses to price the top rigor tier until reconciled, and schedules R-P7RATIO as a 297-record recount; recomputed from spikes/results/p7.jsonl, the numerator is one mandatory run at $9.857 and the denominators differ: the 30-run recommended arm mean $2.693 gives 3.66x (F37) and the same-item recommended run issue-77#r1 at $2.222 gives 4.44x (Decision #33), no running prefix mean of the arm yielding 4.4 [measured]. Neither record states its denominator, which is the whole of the 'contradiction'; ADR-0080's n=1 forbiddance still holds after reconciliation.

concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) [measured] Three rules the design's §0.1 marks DECIDED cite a decision record whose body does not contain them, and grep over references/adr/ finds no record that does. (i) ADR-0011's body decides the two-pack set and the Phase-1 exit bar only — no 'resume', 'init' or CLI text, consumers [] — yet AC-400 (resume-flag denylist), AC-437 (`init` idempotence), design rows 1267/1273/1296/1609 (single `run` entry, no resume flag) and SM-130 :963 ('deterministic resume across kill') cite it, and the §15 table re-titles it 'CLI shape and the Phase 1 exit criterion'. (ii) ADR-0016 decides card delivery and a TTL pin (:35) and is itself partially superseded by ADR-0078, yet AC-095, AC-205, AC-417 and AC-504 carry `decisions: ADR-0016` for the configuration-time StructuredOutput check that §0.1 row 46 marks DECIDED and gates-Phase-1 'Yes'; only ADR-0084 mentions StructuredOutput, as evidence. (iii) ADR-0018 decides rewrite events and the worktree-ownership refusal (:38), yet §0.1 rows 38/39, §5.6 and AC-172..175/AC-183 cite it for 'reconcile() at every entry, and no optimisation that skips it' and the Slice-Verdict trailer axis; proposal §4.5 rule 3 was a consistency rule, never a D-row. After the :6498 title audit ('all ten are corrected') the §15 table also still glosses ADR-0069 as '`unknown` is never ordered against a band', a word absent from that record. Nothing is built wrong — AC-400, F20 with Checkpoint 7c, and AC-172/173 carry the rules into code — but ADR-0085 rule 8 makes the AC→ADR trace mandatory, and the immutability/forbids machinery protects none of the three: an implementer adding a reconcile cache or a `--resume` flag violates no accepted ADR, which is where RUNBOOK Step 8 has already drifted (G05-03). (ii) ADR README:3 rules that 'A decision is cited from here, not from the prose that first argued it.' ADR-0018's Decision (line 38) is rewrite events plus the common-dir/HEAD refusal; its body never mentions tiers as a decision, trailers, `Story:` or `Slice-Verdict:`, and no file under references/adr/ contains 'Slice-Verdict' [measured]. Yet section 0.1 row 38 (a Phase-1-gating DECIDED row) and section 5.4 line 684 say 'A `Slice-Verdict:` axis is therefore required (ADR-0018)', and AC-160 to AC-165 each list 'decisions: ADR-0018'; the tier-1 test and the two-axis rule are decided only in the superseded proposal section 4.5 and RFC section 3.4, restated in design section 5.4. Likewise grep of ADR-0003 for headroom|throttl|rate_limit|utilization returns 0 lines and its forbids block covers ports, git and Postgres only [measured], while section 7.9 (design:1233-1235) attributes three decisions (batch-delta-only headroom, >= 2-tick margins on the visible windows, no cache metric in a headroom figure) to ADR-0003 and AC-372 to AC-381 each carry 'decisions: ADR-0003' (78 such citations register-wide); the only ADR mentioning headroom at all is ADR-0088, incidentally at line 72. Check C (ADR agreement) cannot be performed for either area, and a future supersession of the tier or throttle rule has no record to supersede.

concerns.statement: The advisory table at architecture-design :1697-:1700, repeated in ADR-0084 :19 and evidence-augmentation :160, was reconstructed under a rustsec.org 404 and carries four attributions the advisories do not support [documented, first verification of self-flagged rows]: RUSTSEC-2025-0021 is patched at gix-features >= 0.41.0 (0.71.0 is the gix facade's fixed version, and the adjacent row uses the sub-crate scale, so the column is inconsistent); RUSTSEC-2024-0351 is against gix-ref (>= 0.44.0) and RUSTSEC-2024-0353 against gix-worktree (>= 0.34.0), not `gix`; RUSTSEC-2024-0349's surface is 'crafted tree or blob names' inside a cloned repository, not 'crafted repo names'. ADR-0084 :115's 'no advisory affects `bundled`' is false as an absolute: RUSTSEC-2022-0090 (CVE-2022-35737) is filed against libsqlite3-sys < 0.25.1 precisely because the bundled SQLite carried the CVE. ADR-0084 :19's 'multi-maintainer ... so not a single-author risk' is not what its sources show: crates.io lists one owner (Byron) and no team. Every pin is clear on every item - gix 0.87.1 pulls gix-features ^0.49.1, gix-ref ^0.67.1, gix-worktree ^0.56.0; rusqlite 0.40.2 pulls libsqlite3-sys ^0.38.2 - so this is the record, not the build.

concerns.remediation: Successor erratum record to ADR-0084 (accepted, immutable) correcting :19 and :115: per-crate fixed versions (gix-features >= 0.41.0; gix-ref >= 0.44.0; gix-worktree >= 0.34.0; gix-worktree-state >= 0.17.0), 'crafted tree or blob names', the omitted RUSTSEC-2024-0352 (gix-index) under the existing 'not complete' flag, 'three advisories in the rusqlite family, one (RUSTSEC-2022-0090, libsqlite3-sys < 0.25.1) against bundled SQLite', and 'multi-contributor, single crates.io owner'. Amend architecture-design :1697-:1700/:2015 and evidence-augmentation :160/:162 by dated amendment. Keep `cargo audit` at Step 5.2 as the authoritative check and add `cargo deny` advisories so libsqlite3-sys is covered by lockfile, not by prose.

concerns.title: Four registered-unrun spikes cannot decide their own criterion: S-FACET (auth 0 positives, no surfaces labels), S-CODEX (saturated), S-BIN, P2-B
concerns.statement: S-FACET, the only registered unblock for the derived-facet BLOCKED row and the named source of SM-024's baseline, registers a kill on 'precision >= 0.95 on auth/surfaces and on ui' over the reused 140-cell arm-D label set. Reconstructed from the four label files, that set holds 7 facets x 20 items with no `surfaces` column at all; `auth` has 0 true / 14-16 false / 4 unknown, so its precision is NOT ANSWERABLE (the fault the document names for data_migration only); `ui` has 9 positives, so 9/9 gives a Wilson 95% lower bound of 0.70 and the bar is POWERLESS [measured]. The same document states 27 lines earlier that the 0.95 clause 'is not reachable at n = 20 for any facet however good'; the kill was committed at e642a5b (2026-09-09 16:05) and that result absorbed at a431c62 (22:22) with the kill untouched [measured, git]. The criterion names no estimator (point vs lower bound) and no abstention number, and S-FACET has no METHOD file. S-CODEX (design:1892, 46 dispatches) is shaped on E3 arm (b) over the same 23 fixtures, a comparator the corpus lists as saturated (23/23 vs 23/23, p = 0.625, 'Did not fire'; arm (b)'s FP is also at floor, 0/23), ADR-0007:55 records no pass criterion, and no METHOD file registers it: the only decidable outcome is a regression. S-BIN's METHOD-S section 3.4 rule is single-pass ('2/2 detection and <= 1/3 false positive') while section 3.6 sizes two passes 'for a stability read' with no combination rule (grep for 'both passes|two passes|disagree' returns only line 372) [measured]; the 2026-09-09 amendment re-affirms both 'exactly as registered', and F29 established that verdicts on identical inputs are a weighted coin, so a 2/2-then-1/2 split is the expected case. P2-B exists only as a section 10.5 allocation row (design:1864) naming question, consumers and reason but no criterion form, no n and no positive count; deciding recall >= 0.9 on a Wilson lower bound needs roughly 36 all-positive rows and F40's corpus had 0 of 41 [inferred]. Each is the class golden constraint 10 counts at four, repeated in the registered-unrun set.

concerns.why_before_step5: None of the four is a scheduled RUNBOOK step (phase1-deps.json has zero S-FACET references; S-CODEX is Phase 4; P2-B gates only the stale_policy setting; S-BIN unblocks a slice Step 5.3 already fences), so no Phase-1 block. Each must be fixed before dispatch, because a post-data re-registration is the fault the house rules forbid; S-BIN is the nearest to dispatch.
concerns.remediation: Dated pre-dispatch amendments, registered wording left verbatim (ADR-0012: a named spike with a named consumer, never prose). S-FACET: a METHOD-S2 file or a dated amendment block under change-classification section 6 stating the estimator (Wilson 95% lower bound vs point), the positive count per facet in the reused labels (auth 0, ui 9, surfaces none), declaring `auth` NOT ANSWERABLE and `surfaces` NOT MEASURABLE on this corpus unless a labelled surfaces column is built, fixing the abstention number, and either re-sizing (second corpus, ~60-73 positives per facet) or re-registering the kill on a criterion the 20 items can decide (arm 3 vs arm 1 false-positive count, paired per item). S-CODEX: a METHOD entry before dispatch with a primary metric on a non-saturated measure (S-SUBTLE-tier detection; CLEAN false-positive rate with its Wilson upper bound, noting arm (b)'s 0/23 floor), a stated pass rule and predictions, citing E3 section 9's saturation. S-BIN: a dated METHOD-S section 7 amendment: rule evaluated per pass, branch 1 requires both passes, a pass missing a seed routes to branch 2/3 on that pass's prose, both passes reported. P2-B: a dated METHOD-P amendment (or METHOD-P2B) stating criterion form, the minimum number of blind-labelled 'should re-run' rows, their construction and the cost once sized.

concerns.title: Design section 6.6's durable-systems survey carries wrong cells: Step Functions' 'max activity TTL 6 h' is in no AWS source (the cap is the one-year execution quota), DBOS expires to a sentinel not an error, and Azure Durable mints no token
concerns.statement: Merged from 2 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) Three cells of the cross-system table that ADR-0017's 'single-use plus a deadline is table stakes' conclusion rests on do not match their sources [documented]. (1) architecture-design :841 gives Step Functions 'Server-enforced TTL, max activity TTL 6 h'; neither the SendTaskHeartbeat API page nor the quotas page states 6 h - the developer guide says a waiting task can pause 'until the workflow execution reaches the one year service quota', with HeartbeatSeconds/TimeoutSeconds as opt-in bounds - and the corpus's own grounding-s-results :232 says 'up to the 1-year cap'; 6 h is plausibly the GitHub Actions per-job limit cross-contaminated [inferred]. (2) design-recommendation :86 lists Azure Durable among systems that 'mint a single-use token' with a [1P] tag; first direct verification of the self-flagged row shows Azure external events are addressed by instance ID + event name, mint no token, 'wait indefinitely' unless raced against a durable timer, and are delivered at-least-once. The design :848 row honestly says 'unread'; the recommendation does not. (3) evidence-augmentation :183 files DBOS under 'exception (AWS/DBOS)'; `DBOS.get_event` returns None on timeout - the Inngest sentinel style - and only read_stream raises. The tree-hash-binding conclusion and D17/ADR-0017 survive every correction. (ii) The design's cross-system table (architecture-design §6.3.2) and the evidence-augmentation row it derives from state that AWS Step Functions task tokens carry a 'server-enforced TTL, max activity TTL 6 h'. Neither Step Functions page fetched contains a 6-hour figure: a callback task waits up to the one-year execution quota, and the only tighter deadline is an author-set HeartbeatSeconds/TimeoutSeconds. The same table and its expiry-style paragraph classify DBOS as 'raises an error' on expiry; DBOS's Python and TypeScript docs both say get_event/recv return None/null on timeout, which is the sentinel style the design attributes only to Inngest. The conclusions drawn from the table (single-use tokens, every platform yields a terminal event, nothing binds to a tree hash) are unaffected; the two cells and the 'exception (AWS/DBOS) or sentinel (Inngest)' recommendation are wrong as written. [documented]

concerns.title: ADR-0085 rules 4 and 6 claim 'no external norm at all'; NASA SE Handbook App C/D and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 cover both
concerns.statement: ADR-0085:30 states that two conventions 'have no external norm behind them at all', :112 transcribes the research pass verbatim for rules 4 (an AC names its verifying instrument) and 6 (phrasing a deliberately undecided or blocked item), and architecture-design:153 and :1963 call both 'original process design'. Both have documented first-party antecedents that were live on 2026-09-08. Rule 6 is squarely covered: NASA SE Handbook Appendix C prescribes marking an undecided value 'To Be Resolved' (TBR) 'with the rationale along with what should be done to eliminate the TBR, who is responsible for its elimination, and by when' [documented]; the PROVISIONAL / BLOCKED-AC phrasing extends that convention with an owner gate and a machine-readable state. Rule 4 is covered at requirement grain: Appendix D's Requirements Verification Matrix records, per uniquely identified requirement, the verification method and the evidence document, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148-framed templates carry a per-requirement verification method [documented]. The residue that survives is narrower than the corpus's sentence: the norms name a method class (test, demonstration, inspection, analysis), not a specific test ID, so 'no norm requires naming the instrument itself' may stand [inferred]. ADR-0085's discipline ('absence of a contradicting source is not validation') is intact; only the provenance is wrong.

anchors.quote: - Two of the conventions below have **no external norm behind them at all**, and the record must say so rather than borrow authority it does not have (evidence-augmentation §5).

On the adjacent question behind rule 6: "Is there a convention for phrasing an AC for a deliberately undecided or blocked item so it does not read as an omission? — Nothing found. **No** — a genuine gap in the external literature. Any redkiln practice here is original."

| Is there a documented norm that an acceptance criterion should name its own verifying instrument (test ID, lint rule, metric)? | Nothing first-party or peer-reviewed found; only informal practitioner blog content. |

| Is there a convention for phrasing an AC for a deliberately undecided or blocked item so it does not read as an omission? | Nothing found. | **No** — a genuine gap in the external literature. Any redkiln practice here is original. |

there is **no documented norm that an acceptance criterion should name its own verifying instrument**, so the AC-### + `depends_on` / `tracesTo` convention is **ahead of any external norm rather than confirming one**; and there is **no convention for phrasing an AC

concerns.why_before_step5: No build consequence; the conventions Step 5 follows are unchanged. The record claims originality it does not have, which the house rule at ADR-0085:30 itself forbids.
concerns.remediation: ADR-0085 is accepted: supersede the provenance bullets with a short ADR clause that cites NASA SP-2016-6105 Appendix C (TBD/TBR) as the antecedent rule 6 extends and Appendix D plus ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 verification-method attributes as the antecedent rule 4 specialises, rewording 'original process design' to 'specialises documented requirements-engineering practice; no agile-AC-specific norm found'. Dated erratum to architecture-design §1.4 (:153) and §11 (:1963), and to evidence-augmentation §5 rows 287-288.

concerns.title: `Quarantined` 'no prior art beyond GitLab and Cloudflare' (ADR-0074/0082) is contradicted by SARIF suppressions, Snyk ignore and GitHub dismissal
concerns.statement: Three accepted ADRs and the research pass state that D4's `Quarantined { reason, by, until }` and the Advisory sink have no published prior art beyond two comparators. Four are published and were live on 2026-09-08. OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.35 standardises a suppression object whose `status` is 'accepted', 'underReview' or 'rejected' - 'the disposition of a suppressed result within a result management workflow', i.e. a quarantine state for a disputed finding with two outcomes [documented]. Snyk's `.snyk` ignore carries `--reason` and `--expiry` (default 30 days), field-for-field `Quarantined`'s {reason, until} [documented]. GitHub code-scanning dismissal records a reason and is reopenable; SonarQube has False Positive / Won't Fix / Accepted resolutions [documented]. ADR-0074:100's 'original process design' and ADR-0082:90's 'no part of it should be presented as adopted practice' overstate; 'convergent with SARIF suppression and Snyk ignore-with-expiry' is the honest framing. The Advisory sink's routing of a non-blocking-but-true finding may still be original; that is a different sentence from the one under test [inferred]. No decision changes; an interop option opens.

anchors.quote: - [documented] Clause 6 has **no external prior art beyond GitLab flaky-quarantine and Cloudflare "won't fix"**; the research pass looked and found none (evidence-augmentation §5). `Quarantined` is original process design and should be stated as such.

- No richer prior art exists to copy. GitLab flaky-quarantine and Cloudflare "won't fix" are the only comparators found, and the external research pass records this as a real gap rather than a short-search artefact (evidence-augmentation §5).

D4's `Quarantined` state has no richer prior art to draw on", recorded as a real gap rather than a search artefact. The Advisory sink is therefore **original design**, and no part of it should be presented as adopted practice.

| Are there published quarantine/override patterns for disputed findings beyond GitLab flaky-quarantine and Cloudflare "won't fix"? | Nothing new found; this appears to be a real gap, not a short-search artifact. | **No** — D4's `Quarantined` state has no richer prior art to draw on. |

concerns.why_before_step5: No build consequence for Step 5 (the review gate is a later lane); the record of three accepted ADRs claims a gap that a one-query search closes, and the D4 schema will be written without the SARIF suppression shape in view.
concerns.remediation: Supersede the three provenance bullets with one clause citing SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.35, Snyk ignore, GitHub alert dismissal and SonarQube resolutions as convergent prior art and rewording 'original' to 'convergent'. Register a small design spike (name it D4-SARIF; consumer: the review-gate schema under ADR-0074's successor) to decide whether `Quarantined` maps onto `suppressions[].status` / `justification` for tool interop; until it runs the D4 shape stands. Dated erratum to evidence-augmentation §5 row 292.

concerns.title: The narrowed novelty claim 'in an AI-coding-specific backlog or spec tool' is false: spec-kit, Archon and Bernstein ship persisted human gates
concerns.statement: Evidence-augmentation claim 1 says that none of spec-kit/OpenSpec/BMAD/task-master 'ships an item-kind taxonomy, a stage-gate state machine, or durable approval on a work item', and the design narrows its differentiation claim to 'in an AI-coding-specific backlog or spec tool'. Both were already false at the 2026-09-08 snapshot: spec-kit 1.0.x ships a workflow engine with a `gate` step (approve/reject, on_reject abort/skip/retry), persisted run state under .specify/workflows/runs/<run_id>/ and `specify workflow resume <run_id>` (PR #2158 merged 2026-04-14); Archon has an `approval` node type with `archon workflow approve/resume/reject` and runs persisted in its database (v0.4.0, 2026-05-28); and Bernstein (1,158 stars, created 2026-03-22, absent from the corpus) is a deterministic non-LLM scheduler with task kinds, policy-declared approval and merge gates, a replay journal, worktree-per-task and checkpointed resumable runs, the closest unlisted analogue to the kernel pitch. What survives is narrower than either wording: the gate is attached to a per-invocation run, not to a work item with a kind and a stage machine, and no surveyed system binds the answer to a tree hash. The process-catalog proposal's 'nobody combines an item-kind taxonomy, an executable activity catalog, and deterministic selection' needs a Bernstein row before it can be repeated. [documented]

anchors.quote: The claim that survives is the narrower one: **in an AI-coding-specific backlog or spec tool**, and on the *binding* rather than the gate — redkiln binds the answer to a **tree hash**, which no surveyed system does, Jira included.

concerns.remediation: Reword design line 854 and evidence-augmentation claims 1-2 to the claim that holds: 'no surveyed tool attaches a persisted human gate to a durable work item that carries a kind and a per-kind stage machine, and none binds the answer to a tree hash'. concerns.title: ADR-0081's 'no source frames activity selection as a research question at all' contradicts SME, arXiv 2603.22386 and ADR-0020
concerns.statement: Evidence-augmentation:289 asked for a subfield covering 'LLM-driven' tailoring; ADR-0081:190 restates it as 'no external source frames activity selection as a research question at all', and architecture-design:2026 records 'no comparable published system exists to check this framing against' as a positive result. The unqualified sentence is false three ways. Situational Method Engineering (Henderson-Sellers, Ralyte, Agerfalk and Rossi, Springer 2014) is a book-length field whose central question is which method fragments to select for a situation, using the OPF deontic matrix [documented]; the corpus's own research/2026-09-07-method-engineering.md §3 documents it and ADR-0020:23 cites the OPF deontic matrix as 'prior art for a deontic ordering', so ADR-0081 contradicts an accepted sibling. For the LLM case, arXiv 2603.22386 (2026-03-23) surveys 'workflow optimization for LLM agents', explicitly covering 'dynamic methods, which select, generate, or revise the workflow for a particular run', with AFlow, G-Designer, FlowReasoner and Workflow-R1 as instances [documented]. What survives, narrowed, is 'no published system selects SDLC activities per run from internal quality signals': arXiv 2509.13942 instantiates fixed Waterfall/V/Agile scaffolds and does not select activities, and the verifier's searches for SDLC-specific tailoring returned nothing [documented]. Restore the qualifier and cite the adjacent field.

anchors.quote: that no external source frames activity selection as a research question at all, and names that as a positive gap — no

The research pass looked for a named research subfield covering **LLM-driven process or workflow tailoring** and found none [documented, research pass §5 unresolved]. That is worth recording as a result rather than an absence: **no comparable published system exists to check this framing against**
Search surfaced multi-agent SDLC coordination and lifecycle-aware code generation, but nothing framing activity selection as its own research question.

- Prior art for a deontic ordering exists and is cited directly: the OPF deontic matrix and the V-Modell XT mandatory-modules scheme (V-Modell XT's tailoring is documented as two decades in production).

concerns.why_before_step5: No build consequence; the rigor-ladder decision rests on P7's measurement, not on the absence claim. The record asserts a gap the corpus's own research folder and an accepted ADR contradict.
concerns.remediation: Supersede ADR-0081's 'Corpus versus external evidence' bullet with a clause that restores the 'LLM-driven, per-run, from internal quality signals' qualifier, cites SME (Springer 2014) and arXiv 2603.22386 as the adjacent fields, and cross-references ADR-0020:23. Dated erratum to architecture-design §11 preamble (:2026) and evidence-augmentation §5 row 289, replacing 'no named subfield' with 'nearest fields: SME; agentic workflow optimisation (2603.22386); no SDLC-tailoring system found'.

concerns.title: ADR-0089's 'Semgrep 0.57%-23.8% recall' floor is from a mis-cited arXiv ID (RealVuln: recall 17.5%); two more change-classification rows drift
concerns.statement: change-classification:424 cites arXiv 2604.13764 for 'Dataflow comparator on BigVul/Devign: Semgrep 2.43% F1 / 0.57% recall', :64 repeats the figures, and :9 and accepted ADR-0089:75 and :164 carry the range 'from 0.57% to 23.8% recall' as measured evidence against buying an analysis platform. arXiv 2604.13764 is RealVuln (Pellew and Raza, 2026-04-15), a benchmark over 26 intentionally vulnerable Python repositories in which Semgrep scores F1 18.9, precision 0.205, recall 0.175; 'BigVul', 'Devign', 'dataflow', '2.43' and '0.57' appear nowhere in its abstract, tables, references or PDF, and a web search for the exact figures found no source [documented]. The ID is most likely mis-pasted [inferred]. With RealVuln substituted the measured floor becomes 17.5% recall and the range 17.5%-23.8%, which weakens but does not reverse ADR-0089's argument (CodeQL still publishes no classifier precision or recall; the vocabulary problem still relocates). A second Semgrep figure on the same page drifts: :422's '59.9% IDOR recall' is not in the cited 2025 post but in Semgrep's 27 Aug 2026 Multimodal benchmark post, a different product and study, which the corpus never cites [documented]. Third, :125's 'Nothing found, positive or negative. The 0/20 result has no literature to compare against' for data-migration classification is answered by the schema/code co-evolution literature: Qiu, Li and Su (ESEC/FSE 2013) detect schema-changing revisions across 160K revisions in ten applications by the same schema-file detection the corpus's DECLARED migrations directory uses, then validate by hand, giving a base rate of roughly 1.7% of revisions touching schema (about 0.9% real) [documented]; at that rate 0 positives in 20 items is the expected outcome, which is the number the design's NOT MEASURABLE row (architecture-design:19) lacks to say how many items a decidable `data_migration` criterion needs [inferred].

concerns.statement: Merged from 3 concerns; each member statement is carried verbatim. (i) None of these changes a live decision; each is a record defect in a document the live set cites as history or evidence [documented]. (a) evidence-augmentation :34 quotes the vendor's compaction guidance as 'nuanced understanding that took an entire session to build' under a [1P] tag; the phrase is on no first-party page (six raw pages grepped) and only in third-party blogs; the substantive point at architecture-design :76 is carried by the page's 'intermediate reasoning are gone'. (b) github-platform :73 and verification :9 call 2,000 points/min the GraphQL 'primary limit'; it is a secondary per-endpoint limit and the primary is 5,000 points/hour per user - a 24x error for anyone capacity-planning a GitHub adapter. (c) competitive-workflows :42 'custom types still not GA as of the docs read' was false on the read date: GA in GitLab 19.1 (2026-06-18). (d) github-platform :43 'GitHub doesn't publish one number' is false (50,000 items) and ~1,200 has been obsolete since Feb 2024. (e) Dead at write time: grounding-s-results :296 (beads docs/ADVANCED.md, removed 2026-07-12) and architecture-proposal :425 (beads docs/WORKTREES.md, moved 2026-07-11); github-platform :46's blog slug 404s. (f) Statuses already false when written: 'Open issue #4214' (closed 2026-08-03), Backlog.md 'Known issue #558' (closed 2026-06-17), and the 'GitHub Action variant' there is Nulab Backlog, not Backlog.md. (g) github-platform :13 names the `issues` webhook for sub-issue actions; they arrive on `sub_issues`. (h) Misattributions: the 41-spec-files anecdote (workflow-model :44) is TrueFoundry's, on neither cited page; 'Firesmith & Henderson-Sellers' links a sole-author Henderson-Sellers 2002 article; Archon #901 predates the rewrite and contains no complaint; OpenAI's moderation post does describe an optional distillation step; wshobson/agents' Gemini CLI path was replaced by Antigravity CLI on 2026-08-18 and Aeon claims nine harnesses, not six. (ii) Research-only documents, none re-cited for these figures by a live document [measured: grep of RUNBOOK, design, AC/SM registers and ADRs], carry numbers their sources do not contain. grounding-s-results:262 credits arXiv 2402.11048 with '~93% say most docs are incomplete or outdated' [P]; the paper is an Ericsson defect analysis of 101 bug reports whose only shares are 30%, 17% and 59%, and the 93% most plausibly belongs to Aghajani et al.'s ICSE 2019 survey it cites [documented/inferred]. workflow-model:44's 'documented case of 41 spec files across 9 repos ... nine AGENTS.md variants' is in neither cited page; it is a TrueFoundry post that presents the figures as an illustrative narrative about 'an engineering manager named Bastien', so 'documented case' is contradicted by the source's own words [documented]. grounding-s-results:293 points 'Martian benchmark' at arXiv 2603.26130, which is Foundry AI's SWE-PRBench (350 PRs, 15-31% recall), not Martian's Code Review Bench (200k-300k PRs, ~56% precision) described at :252 [documented]. competitive-workflows:148's 'another lists 2,300+' is on no version of the kissmyskills page (figures present: 1,000+, 2,000+, 42,816+) [documented]. method-engineering:22's 'Method Composer 7.6.x (GA Dec 2020)' is dated 20 Mar 2020 (7.6) / Jul 2020 (7.6.1) by the cited IBM page [documented]. workflow-model:15's '~10/25/55/10' RUP effort curve and OpenUP 'practice' concept are on neither the cited GeeksforGeeks page (five phases, no percentages) nor any cited source [documented]. Separately, the self-flagged UNVERIFIED item at shipmates-status:8 ('Cargo.toml on main still reads 0.1.12') is now first-verified: the commit that set 0.1.19 is dated 2026-09-01T20:48Z, before the 2026-09-03 pass, so the observation was a crawl artefact and the 'Avoid (4): Cargo.toml lagging release tags' lesson at :39 rests on nothing [documented]. (iii) Thirty-one drifts confined to research-only or superseded documents, none of which a live document re-cites for the drifted claim [measured] (ADR-0028 cites Prifti as prior art by name only; ADR-0031 cites workflow-model §2, not the drifted rows). Dead or withdrawn: change-classification:495's JMLR PDF path 404s (live path /papers/volume11/el-yaniv10a/el-yaniv10a.pdf); :505's Greptile post is 410 Gone (Wayback 2025-08-04 confirms the claim); workflow-model:17's faros.ai summary 301s to the blog index; workflow-model:7's iso.org/standard/63712 is the withdrawn 2017 edition, revised by ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026 (April 2026, before the pass) [documented]. Superseded pins: arXiv 2606.20615v2 (v3 2026-08-16, three authors, adds a SWE-bench section), arXiv 2411.13768v2 (v3 retitled 'Evaluation-Driven Development and Operations of LLM Agents'), and the Azure DevOps cmmi-process page rewritten 2026-06-22 so that competitive-workflows:28's quotes now live on the sibling cmmi-process-workflow page [documented]. Paraphrase in quotation marks: method-engineering:82 'limited guidance on how teams integrate' (HELENA, in neither PDF), selection-and-planning:255 'a working agreement, not a strict set of rules' (page says 'Regard the criteria as guidelines, not strict rules'), method-engineering:13 'descriptors' (EPF/RMC vocabulary, not SPEM 2.0's 'Method Content Use'), :63 'producers perform work units, work units maintain work products' (not in the SEI PDF) [documented]. Tag, venue and characterisation: [blog] for a theory preprint (change-classification:418), 'Yih' for 'Yu' (:484), 'image classification only' for a paper with a tabular regression task (:496), 'FSE-Industry 2024' for AIware '24 (grounding-s-results:147), [preprint] for an EASE 2026 paper (:326), ChatDev phases attributed to a survey that does not list them (method-engineering:120), 2511.09794 credited with 2509.13942's 132-run numbers (:122), 'preferred minimal conflict sets' in neither cited ASP paper (selection-and-planning:105), 'more understandable' for a size/complexity-versus-modularity trade-off (method-engineering:106), a 2024 caveat paper cited as support for 'easy' SAT (selection-and-planning:111), Kubernetes 'named triage owners' where ownership is by SIG (change-classification:469), Dynamic Workflows on 'Pro' at a launch whose sources list Max/Team/Enterprise/API (verification:10), Jira sprawl 'per type per project' and 'validators' where the source says per project and conditions (competitive-workflows:18), BMAD token-cost and v4-to-v6 churn not in the cited sources (:80), LogRocket cited for complaints its tutorial does not contain (:90), two of three Kiro complaints unsupported (:99), Dev Genius's 'missing link' being spec-to-code traceability, not a cross-harness selector (:193), and the superseded architecture-proposal:423 writing 'RunTests' and attributing -NullRHI to Epic pages that do not carry it [documented]. Substance survives in every case; the fixes are wording, tags and URLs.

verdict: The corpus is ready to build from at Step 5, on one reading: no concern is P0. Nothing found makes Step 5 write the wrong crate, and every dependency on something unrun or absent is fenced by a checkpoint, a legend line or an ADR reading resolvable on the page. What held is substantial [measured]: the census reproduced the id namespaces, the ADR graph, the area tallies and most restated numbers; 697 of 860 external claims were confirmed live on 2026-09-10 (105 drifted, 29 contradicted, 16 unverifiable, 13 stale by date); every crate pin is clear of every advisory; 1,381 self-recorded issues absorb 69 of these 110 concerns as sharpenings, not discoveries. Seventeen P1s must be settled before or at Step 5. Sequencing: the three LLM boolean facets have no disposition between Step 4's rule and Checkpoint 4a (PIA-003); AC-520 has no passing route and Phase-0 exit (c) is read three ways (PIA-001); the corpus Steps 6-7 test against is neither moved by Step 2 nor reachable from the pinned SHA (PIA-002). Contracts Step 5.3 snapshots: the closed-output schema rules cannot all hold and StepError is unenumerated (PIA-005); Findings.repro has no mutant field (PIA-007); the companion kind list is unsettled (PIA-006); no Rust toolchain adapter exists for the self-hosting exit (PIA-004). Contracts the next steps build to: memo tier and keys (PIA-008), common-dir on gix (PIA-009), the Harness port's dispatch/cancel (PIA-010), pack authoring's missing step (PIA-011), six adapter-level decisions (PIA-012 to PIA-017). Each is a decision by record, never an edit. The 82 P2s carry no build consequence and batch into four passes: Step-5 manifest and checkpoint fixes (PIA-023 to PIA-039); one erratum record per affected accepted ADR (0077, 0083/0085, 0084, 0086, 0087, 0088, 0089); a dated-correction pass over statistics and baselines (PIA-073 to PIA-078); a closeout pass over ranges, ids and un-propagated corrections (PIA-070, PIA-075). No P0 is a finding about fences, not a clean bill: eighteen rk-git behaviours are left to the implementer (PIA-040), 41 of 110 concerns are new to the corpus, and five sizing figures are powerless at their own n (PIA-073).
